 }\n}\n\nfn index_of(data: &Value) -> Result<usize, LlmError> {\n    data.get(\"index\").and_then(Value::as_u64).map(|i| i as usize).ok_or_else(|| LlmError::Protocol(\"content block event without an index\".into()))\n}\n\nfn stop_reason(reason: &str) -> StopReason {\n    match reason {\n        \"end_turn\" => StopReason::EndTurn,\n        \"tool_use\" => StopReason::ToolUse,\n        \"max_tokens\" => StopReason::MaxTokens,\n        \"refusal\" => StopReason::Refusal,\n        other => StopReason::Other(other.to_string()),\n    }\n}\n"

  "content": "//! OpenAI Chat Completions (`POST {base}/chat/completions`, streaming) and every server that\n//! speaks it: Ollama, the MaluOS gateway, vLLM, LM Studio.\n//!\n//! Two flavours differ in one field: OpenAI's own API takes `max_completion_tokens` and\n//! `reasoning_effort`; compatible servers take `max_tokens` and get no effort field.\n\nuse std::sync::Arc;\n\nuse serde_json::{Map, Value, json};\n\nuse crate::sse::{SseEvent, read_events};\nuse crate::transport::{HttpRequest, Transport, error_from_response};\nuse crate::{Completion, ContentBlock, Effort, Event, Flow, LlmClient, LlmError, Message, Request, Role, StopReason, Usage};\n\npub const OPENAI_BASE_URL: &str = \"https://api.openai.com/v1\";\npub const OLLAMA_BASE_URL: &str = \"http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1\";\n/// The model used when the caller names none.\npub const DEFAULT_MODEL: &str = \"gpt-5.1\";\n\n/// Which dialect of the protocol the server speaks.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum Flavor {\n    /// api.openai.com: `max_completion_tokens`, `reasoning_effort`.\n    OpenAi,\n    /// Ollama, the MaluOS gateway and other compatible servers: `max_tokens`.\n    Compatible,\n}\n\n/// A client for one server.\npub struct OpenAiClient {\n    transport: Arc<dyn Transport>,\n    base_url: String,\n    api_key: Option<String>,\n    flavor: Flavor,\n    provider: String,\n}\n\nimpl OpenAiClient {\n    /// OpenAI's own API.\n    pub fn openai(transport: Arc<dyn Transport>, api_key: impl Into<String>) -> Self {\n        OpenAiClient { transport, base_url: OPENAI_BASE_URL.into(), api_key: Some(api_key.into()), flavor: Flavor::OpenAi, provider: \"openai\".into() }\n    }\n\n    /// OpenAI with the native transport and the key from the environment ([`crate::keys`]).\n    #[cfg(all(feature = \"native\", not(target_arch = \"wasm32\")))]\n    pub fn openai_from_env() -> Result<Self, LlmError> {\n        let key = crate::keys::api_key_from_env(crate::keys::Provider::OpenAi)?;\n        Ok(Self::openai(Arc::new(crate::UreqTransport::default()), key))\n    }\n\n    /// Any compatible server. `base_url` includes the `/v1` (or whatever prefix the server uses);\n    /// `api_key` is sent as a bearer token when given.\n    pub fn compatible(transport: Arc<dyn Transport>, provider: impl Into<String>, base_url: impl Into<String>, api_key: Option<String>) -> Self {\n        let mut base_url: String = base_url.into();\n        while base_url.ends_with('/') {\n            base_url.pop();\n        }\n        OpenAiClient { transport, base_url, api_key, flavor: Flavor::Compatible, provider: provider.into() }\n    }\n\n    /// A local Ollama at its default address.\n    pub fn ollama(transport: Arc<dyn Transport>) -> Self {\n        Self::compatible(transport, \"ollama\", OLLAMA_BASE_URL, None)\n    }\n\n    pub fn flavor(&self) -> Flavor {\n        self.flavor\n    }\n\n    /// The HTTP request for `request`, as it would be sent.\n    pub fn build_request(&self, request: &Request) -> HttpRequest {\n        let mut body = Map::new();\n        body.insert(\"model\".into(), Value::String(request.model.clone()));\n        body.insert(\"messages\".into(), Value::Array(messages_json(request)));\n        body.insert(\"stream\".into(), Value::Bool(true));\n        body.insert(\"stream_options\".into(), json!({\"include_usage\": true}));\n        let max_key = match self.flavor {\n            Flavor::OpenAi => \"max_completion_tokens\",\n            Flavor::Compatible => \"max_tokens\",\n        };\n        body.insert(max_key.into(), json!(request.max_tokens));\n        if !request.tools.is_empty() {\n            let tools = request\n                .tools\n                .iter()\n                .map(|t| json!({\"type\": \"function\", \"function\": {\"name\": t.name, \"description\": t.description, \"parameters\": t.input_schema}}))\n                .collect();\n            body.insert(\"tools\".into(), Value::Array(tools));\n        }\n        if let (Flavor::OpenAi, Some(effort)) = (self.flavor, request.effort) {\n            let effort = match effort {\n                Effort::Low => \"low\",\n                Effort::Medium => \"medium\",\n                Effort::High | Effort::XHigh | Effort::Max => \"high\",\n            };\n            body.insert(\"reasoning_effort\".into(), Value::String(effort.into()));\n        }\n        let mut headers = vec![(\"content-type\".to_string(), \"application/json\".to_string())];\n        if let Some(key) = &self.api_key {\n            headers.push((\"authorization\".to_string(), format!(\"Bearer {key}\")));\n        }\n        HttpRequest { url: format!(\"{}/chat/completions\", self.base_url), headers, body: Value::Object(body).to_string() }\n    }\n}\n\nfn messages_json(request: &Request) -> Vec<Value> {\n    let mut out = Vec::new();\n    if let Some(system) = &request.system {\n        out.push(json!({\"role\": \"system\", \"content\": system}));\n    }\n    for message in &request.messages {\n        match message.role {\n            Role::User => user_json(message, &mut out),\n            Role::Assistant => out.push(assistant_json(message)),\n        }\n    }\n    out\n}\n\n/// Text blocks become one `user` message; each tool result is its own `tool` message, in the\n/// order the blocks have.\nfn user_json(message: &Message, out: &mut Vec<Value>) {\n    let mut text = String::new();\n    let flush = |text: &mut String, out: &mut Vec<Value>| {\n        if !text.is_empty() {\n            out.push(json!({\"role\": \"user\", \"content\": std::mem::take(text)}));\n        }\n    };\n    for block in &message.content {\n        match block {\n            ContentBlock::Text { text: t } => text.push_str(t),\n            ContentBlock::ToolResult { tool_use_id, content, .. } => {\n                flush(&mut text, out);\n                out.push(json!({\"role\": \"tool\", \"tool_call_id\": tool_use_id, \"content\": content}));\n            }\n            ContentBlock::Thinking { .. } | ContentBlock::ToolUse { .. } | ContentBlock::Raw { .. } => {}\n        }\n    }\n    flush(&mut text, out);\n}\n\nfn assistant_json(message: &Message) -> Value {\n    let mut text = String::new();\n    let mut tool_calls = Vec::new();\n    for block in &message.content {\n        match block {\n            ContentBlock::Text { text: t } => text.push_str(t),\n            ContentBlock::ToolUse { id, name, input } => {\n                tool_calls.push(json!({\"id\": id, \"type\": \"function\", \"function\": {\"name\": name, \"arguments\": input.to_string()}}));\n            }\n            ContentBlock::Thinking { .. } | ContentBlock::ToolResult { .. } | ContentBlock::Raw { .. } => {}\n        }\n    }\n    let mut v = Map::new();\n    v.insert(\"role\".into(), \"assistant\".into());\n    v.insert(\"content\".into(), if text.is_empty() { Value::Null } else { Value::String(text) });\n    if !tool_calls.is_empty() {\n        v.insert(\"tool_calls\".into(), Value::Array(tool_calls));\n    }\n    Value::Object(v)\n}\n\nimpl LlmClient for OpenAiClient {\n    fn provider(&self) -> &str {\n        &self.provider\n    }\n\n    fn complete(&self, request: &Request, on_event: &mut dyn FnMut(Event) -> Flow) -> Result<Completion, LlmError> {\n        let http = self.build_request(request);\n        let response = self.transport.post(&http)?;\n        if !(200..300).contains(&response.status) {\n            return Err(error_from_response(response));\n        }\n        let mut stream = Stream::new(request.model.clone());\n        read_events(response.body, &mut |event| stream.handle(event, on_event))?;\n        stream.finish()\n    }\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug)]\nenum Block {\n    Text(String),\n    Thinking(String),\n    ToolCall { id: String, name: String, arguments: String, started: bool },\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug)]\nstruct Stream {\n    model: String,\n    blocks: Vec<Block>,\n    /// Block position of each tool call index.\n    calls: Vec<usize>,\n    stop: Option<StopReason>,\n    usage: Usage,\n    done: bool,\n}\n\nimpl Stream {\n    fn new(model: String) -> Self {\n        Stream { model, blocks: Vec::new(), calls: Vec::new(), stop: None, usage: Usage::default(), done: false }\n    }\n\n    fn handle(&mut self, event: SseEvent, on_event: &mut dyn FnMut(Event) -> Flow) -> Result<Flow, LlmError> {\n        if event.data.trim() == \"[DONE]\" {\n            self.done = true;\n            return Ok(Flow::Continue);\n        }\n        let chunk: Value = serde_json::from_str(&event.data).map_err(|e| LlmError::Protocol(format!(\"chunk is not JSON: {e}\")))?;\n        if let Some(error) = chunk.get(\"error\") {\n            let message = error.get(\"message\").and_then(Value::as_str).unwrap_or(\"no details\").to_string();\n            let code = error.get(\"code\").and_then(Value::as_u64).map(|c| c as u16);\n            return Err(match code {\n                Some(status) => LlmError::from_status(status, message),\n                None => LlmError::Protocol(crate::error_message(&chunk.to_string())),\n            });\n        }\n        if let Some(model) = chunk.get(\"model\").and_then(Value::as_str) {\n            self.model = model.to_string();\n        }\n        if let Some(usage) = chunk.get(\"usage\").filter(|u| u.is_object()) {\n            let get = |key: &str| usage.get(key).and_then(Value::as_u64).unwrap_or(0);\n            self.usage.input_tokens = get(\"prompt_tokens\");\n            self.usage.output_tokens = get(\"completion_tokens\");\n            self.usage.cache_read_input_tokens = usage.get(\"prompt_tokens_details\").and_then(|d| d.get(\"cached_tokens\")).and_then(Value::as_u64).unwrap_or(0);\n            if on_event(Event::Usage(self.usage)) == Flow::Stop {\n                return Ok(Flow::Stop);\n            }\n        }\n        let Some(choice) = chunk.get(\"choices\").and_then(Value::as_array).and_then(|c| c.first()) else {\n            return Ok(Flow::Continue);\n        };\n        if let Some(reason) = choice.get(\"finish_reason\").and_then(Value::as_str) {\n            self.stop = Some(match reason {\n                \"stop\" => StopReason::EndTurn,\n                \"tool_calls\" | \"function_call\" => StopReason::ToolUse,\n                \"length\" => StopReason::MaxTokens,\n                \"content_filter\" => StopReason::Refusal,\n                other => StopReason::Other(other.to_string()),\n            });\n        }\n        let Some(delta) = choice.get(\"delta\") else {\n            return Ok(Flow::Continue);\n        };\n        for key in [\"reasoning_content\", \"reasoning\"] {\n            if let Some(piece) = delta.get(key).and_then(Value::as_str).filter(|s| !s.is_empty()) {\n                match self.blocks.last_mut() {\n                    Some(Block::Thinking(text)) => text.push_str(piece),\n                    _ => self.blocks.push(Block::Thinking(piece.to_string())),\n                }\n                if on_event(Event::ThinkingDelta(piece.to_string())) == Flow::Stop {\n                    return Ok(Flow::Stop);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        if let Some(piece) = delta.get(\"content\").and_then(Value::as_str).filter(|s| !s.is_empty()) {\n            match self.blocks.last_mut() {\n                Some(Block::Text(text)) => text.push_str(piece),\n                _ => self.blocks.push(Block::Text(piece.to_string())),\n            }\n            if on_event(Event::TextDelta(piece.to_string())) == Flow::Stop {\n                return Ok(Flow::Stop);\n            }\n        }\n        if let Some(calls) = delta.get(\"tool_calls\").and_then(Value::as_array) {\n            for call in calls {\n                if self.tool_call_delta(call, on_event)? == Flow::Stop {\n                    return Ok(Flow::Stop);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        Ok(Flow::Continue)\n    }\n\n    fn tool_call_delta(&mut self, call: &Value, on_event: &mut dyn FnMut(Event) -> Flow) -> Result<Flow, LlmError> {\n        let index = call.get(\"index\").and_then(Value::as_u64).map(|i| i as usize).unwrap_or(self.calls.len().saturating_sub(1));\n        if index > self.calls.len() {\n            return Err(LlmError::Protocol(format!(\"tool call {index} before tool call {}\", self.calls.len())));\n        }\n        if index == self.calls.len() {\n            self.calls.push(self.blocks.len());\n            self.blocks.push(Block::ToolCall { id: String::new(), name: String::new(), arguments: String::new(), started: false });\n        }\n        let position = self.calls[index];\n        let Some(Block::ToolCall { id, name, arguments, started }) = self.blocks.get_mut(position) else {\n            return Err(LlmError::Protocol(format!(\"tool call {index} lost its block\")));\n        };\n        if let Some(piece) = call.get(\"id\").and_then(Value::as_str) {\n            id.push_str(piece);\n        }\n        let function = call.get(\"function\").cloned().unwrap_or(Value::Null);\n        if let Some(piece) = function.get(\"name\").and_then(Value::as_str) {\n            name.push_str(piece);\n        }\n        if !*started && !name.is_empty() {\n            *started = true;\n            if on_event(Event::ToolUseStart { index: position, id: id.clone(), name: name.clone() }) == Flow::Stop {\n                return Ok(Flow::Stop);\n            }\n        }\n        if let Some(piece) = function.get(\"arguments\").and_then(Value::as_str).filter(|s| !s.is_empty()) {\n            arguments.push_str(piece);\n            if on_event(Event::ToolInputDelta { index: position, partial_json: piece.to_string() }) == Flow::Stop {\n                return Ok(Flow::Stop);\n            }\n        }\n        Ok(Flow::Continue)\n    }\n\n    fn finish(self) -> Result<Completion, LlmError> {\n        let Some(mut stop_reason) = self.stop else {\n            return Err(LlmError::Protocol(if self.done { \"the stream carried no finish_reason\".into() } else { \"the stream ended early\".into() }));\n        };\n        let mut content = Vec::with_capacity(self.blocks.len());\n        for block in self.blocks {\n            content.push(match block {\n                Block::Text(text) => ContentBlock::Text { text },\n                Block::Thinking(text) => ContentBlock::Thinking { text, signature: None },\n                Block::ToolCall { id, name, arguments, .. } => {\n                    let input = if arguments.trim().is_empty() {\n                        Value::Object(Map::new())\n                    } else {\n                        serde_json::from_str(&arguments).map_err(|e| LlmError::Protocol(format!(\"tool `{name}` arguments are not valid JSON: {e}\")))?\n                    };\n                    if stop_reason == StopReason::EndTurn {\n                        // Some servers report `stop` even when they called a tool.\n                        stop_reason = StopReason::ToolUse;\n                    }\n                    ContentBlock::ToolUse { id, name, input }\n                }\n            });\n        }\n        Ok(Completion { model: self.model, content, stop_reason, usage: self.usage })\n    }\n}\n"

Scripted replacements for tests: a [`MockTransport`] that answers posts with canned HTTP\n//! replies (to test a backend's wire format and parser) and a [`MockClient`] that answers\n//! requests with canned completions (to test whatever drives an [`LlmClient`]).\n\nuse std::collections::VecDeque;\nuse std::io::Cursor;\nuse std::sync::Mutex;\n\nuse crate::transport::{HttpRequest, HttpResponse, Transport};\nuse crate::{Completion, ContentBlock, Event, Flow, LlmClient, LlmError, Request};\n\n/// One canned HTTP reply.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct Reply {\n    pub status: u16,\n    pub headers: Vec<(String, String)>,\n    pub body: String,\n}\n\n/// Answers each post with the next scripted reply and records every request.\n#[derive(Debug, Default)]\npub struct MockTransport {\n    replies: Mutex<VecDeque<Reply>>,\n    requests: Mutex<Vec<HttpRequest>>,\n}\n\nimpl MockTransport {\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        Self::default()\n    }\n\n    /// Queue a reply with the given status and body.\n    pub fn reply(&self, status: u16, body: impl Into<String>) -> &Self {\n        self.reply_with_headers(status, Vec::new(), body)\n    }\n\n    pub fn reply_with_headers(&self, status: u16, headers: Vec<(String, String)>, body: impl Into<String>) -> &Self {\n        self.replies.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()).push_back(Reply { status, headers, body: body.into() });\n        self\n    }\n\n    /// Every request posted so far, in order.\n    pub fn requests(&self) -> Vec<HttpRequest> {\n        self.requests.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()).clone()\n    }\n\n    /// The JSON body of the last request.\n    pub fn last_body(&self) -> Option<serde_json::Value> {\n        self.requests().last().and_then(|r| serde_json::from_str(&r.body).ok())\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Transport for MockTransport {\n    fn post(&self, request: &HttpRequest) -> Result<HttpResponse, LlmError> {\n        self.requests.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()).push(request.clone());\n        let reply = self.replies.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()).pop_front();\n        match reply {\n            Some(reply) => Ok(HttpResponse { status: reply.status, headers: reply.headers, body: Box::new(Cursor::new(reply.body.into_bytes())) }),\n            None => Err(LlmError::Transport(\"mock transport: no scripted reply left\".into())),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Server-Sent Events text from (event name, data) pairs; an empty name gives a bare `data:`\n/// line (OpenAI's style).\npub fn sse(events: &[(&str, &str)]) -> String {\n    let mut out = String::new();\n    for (event, data) in events {\n        if !event.is_empty() {\n            out.push_str(\"event: \");\n            out.push_str(event);\n            out.push('\\n');\n        }\n        out.push_str(\"data: \");\n        out.push_str(data);\n        out.push_str(\"\\n\\n\");\n    }\n    out\n}\n\n/// Answers each request with the next scripted completion, replaying its blocks as events,\n/// and records every request.\n#[derive(Debug, Default)]\npub struct MockClient {\n    completions: Mutex<VecDeque<Result<Completion, LlmError>>>,\n    requests: Mutex<Vec<Request>>,\n}\n\nimpl MockClient {\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        Self::default()\n    }\n\n    pub fn push(&self, completion: Completion) -> &Self {\n        self.completions.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()).push_back(Ok(completion));\n        self\n    }\n\n    pub fn push_error(&self, error: LlmError) -> &Self {\n        self.completions.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()).push_back(Err(error));\n        self\n    }\n\n    /// Every request made so far, in order.\n    pub fn requests(&self) -> Vec<Request> {\n        self.requests.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()).clone()\n    }\n}\n\nimpl LlmClient for MockClient {\n    fn provider(&self) -> &str {\n        \"mock\"\n    }\n\n    fn complete(&self, request: &Request, on_event: &mut dyn FnMut(Event) -> Flow) -> Result<Completion, LlmError> {\n        self.requests.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()).push(request.clone());\n        let next = self.completions.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()).pop_front();\n        let completion = match next {\n            Some(Ok(c)) => c,\n            Some(Err(e)) => return Err(e),\n            None => return Err(LlmError::Transport(\"mock client: no scripted completion left\".into())),\n        };\n        for (index, block) in completion.content.iter().enumerate() {\n            let flow = match block {\n                ContentBlock::Text { text } => on_event(Event::TextDelta(text.clone())),\n                ContentBlock::Thinking { text, .. } => on_event(Event::ThinkingDelta(text.clone())),\n                ContentBlock::ToolUse { id, name, input } => {\n                    if on_event(Event::ToolUseStart { index, id: id.clone(), name: name.clone() }) == Flow::Stop {\n                        return Err(LlmError::Cancelled);\n                    }\n                    on_event(Event::ToolInputDelta { index, partial_json: input.to_string() })\n                }\n                ContentBlock::ToolResult { .. } | ContentBlock::Raw { .. } => Flow::Continue,\n            };\n            if flow == Flow::Stop {\n                return Err(LlmError::Cancelled);\n            }\n        }\n        if on_event(Event::Usage(completion.usage)) == Flow::Stop {\n            return Err(LlmError::Cancelled);\n        }\n        Ok(completion)\n    }\n}\n"

Default model `gpt-5.1`. |\n| `OpenAiClient::compatible` / `::ollama` | `POST {base}/chat/completions` | For Ollama (`http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1`, no key), the MaluOS gateway, vLLM, LM Studio: `max_tokens`, no effort field, bearer token only when a key is given. `reasoning_content`/`reasoning` deltas become `ThinkingDelta`. A tool call reported with `finish_reason: stop` still yields `StopReason::ToolUse`. |\n| `mock::MockClient` | none | Scripted completions replayed as events; records requests. ## 🤖 Claude

Phase 3.1 is done, committed as `736a57a8` and pushed to `origin main`.

**What landed.** A new crate, `crates/maluos-llm`, at layer 5 of the workspace. It is small and synchronous, with no async runtime and no vendor SDK, which fits the engine's hand-written style and the wasm gate.

- One trait, `LlmClient::complete`, takes a provider-neutral request and streams events while the answer arrives. The callback can cancel. The result is the whole completion with its stop reason and token usage.
- The Anthropic backend speaks the Messages API at version 2026-10-21 with streaming, tools, effort, and thinking blocks passed back signed. Refusal fallbacks are on by default, so a safety decline is re-run on another model inside the same call. Turn that off with one builder call if you prefer.
- The OpenAI backend has two flavours. The OpenAI one sends `max_completion_tokens` and a reasoning effort. The compatible one serves Ollama, the MaluOS gateway, vLLM and LM Studio, so Ollama support is already in place even though the plan put it later.
- Keys come from `MALUOS_SLIDES_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, and the same pattern for OpenAI. Nothing reads a settings file or a deck.
- A mock transport and a mock client give the next steps scripted, network-free tests.

**Verification.** 16 tests pass, clippy is clean under the crate-level denies, rustfmt, the layering check, the asset check and the wasm32 check all pass. The full description is in `docs/maluos-slides/llm.md`.

**One part of the step's own "done when" is not met.** The plan asked for a run against the demo agent on the dev VM. The gateway socket is a Unix socket with a protocol not documented in this tree, and no Ollama is installed here, so there has been no live request yet. The mocks cover the wire format. A real check needs one of these from you:

- an Anthropic or OpenAI key exported in the shell, or
- Ollama installed on this machine with one model pulled, or
- the gateway's protocol, so I can write the small Unix-socket transport.

Next is step 3.3, the tool schema generated from the command catalog so MCP and the assistant share one table, then 3.2, the deck context builder.

/// Which dialect of the protocol the server speaks.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Flavor {
    /// api.openai.com: `max_completion_tokens`, `reasoning_effort`.
    OpenAi,
    /// Ollama, the MaluOS gateway and other compatible servers: `max_tokens`.
    Compatible,
}

/// A client for one server.
pub struct OpenAiClient {
    transport: Arc<dyn Transport>,
    base_url: String,
    api_key: Option<String>,
    flavor: Flavor,
    provider: String,
}

impl OpenAiClient {
    /// OpenAI's own API.
    pub fn openai(transport: Arc<dyn Transport>, api_key: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        OpenAiClient { transport, base_url: OPENAI_BASE_URL.into(), api_key: Some(api_key.into()), flavor: Flavor::OpenAi, provider: "openai".into() }
    }

    /// OpenAI with the native transport and the key from the environment ([`crate::keys`]).
    #[cfg(all(feature = "native", not(target_arch = "wasm32")))]
    pub fn openai_from_env() -> Result<Self, LlmError> {
        let key = crate::keys::api_key_from_env(crate::keys::Provider::OpenAi)?;
        Ok(Self::openai(Arc::new(crate::UreqTransport::default()), key))
    }

    /// Any compatible server. `base_url` includes the `/v1` (or whatever prefix the server uses);
    /// `api_key` is sent as a bearer token when given.
    pub fn compatible(transport: Arc<dyn Transport>, provider: impl Into<String>, base_url: impl Into<String>, api_key: Option<String>) -> Self {
        let mut base_url: String = base_url.into();
        while base_url.ends_with('/') {
            base_url.pop();
        }
        OpenAiClient { transport, base_url, api_key, flavor: Flavor::Compatible, provider: provider.into() }
    }

    /// A local Ollama at its default address.
    pub fn ollama(transport: Arc<dyn Transport>) -> Self {
        Self::compatible(transport, "ollama", OLLAMA_BASE_URL, None)
    }

    pub fn flavor(&self) -> Flavor {
        self.flavor
    }

    /// The HTTP request for `request`, as it would be sent.
---

    /// The assistant message to append to the conversation before the next request.
    pub fn as_message(&self) -> Message {
        Message { role: Role::Assistant, content: self.content.clone() }
    }
}

/// What a backend reports while the answer streams in. Text and tool input arrive in pieces;
/// the [`Completion`] returned at the end has them whole.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub enum Event {
    TextDelta(String),
    ThinkingDelta(String),
    ToolUseStart {
        index: usize,
        id: String,
        name: String,
    },
    ToolInputDelta {
        index: usize,
        partial_json: String,
    },
    /// Usage so far (providers report input tokens first, output tokens at the end).
    Usage(Usage),
}

/// The event callback's answer: keep streaming, or stop and return [`LlmError::Cancelled`].
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Flow {
    Continue,
    Stop,
}

/// What can go wrong. [`LlmError::retryable`] tells a loop whether waiting and trying again
/// makes sense.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, thiserror::Error)]

Sends one prompt with one tool, streams the answer to stdout, then answers the tool call so\n//! the whole exchange (request, stream, tool use, tool result) is exercised once.\n\nuse std::io::Write;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\n\nuse maluos_llm::{\n    AnthropicClient, ContentBlock, Event, Flow, LlmClient, LlmError, Message, OpenAiClient, Request, StopReason, ToolDef, UreqTransport,\n};\n\nfn usage() -> ! {\n    eprintln!(\"usage: live ollama <model> | anthropic [model] | openai [model] | compatible <base_url> <model>\");\n    std::process::exit(2)\n}\n\nfn client(args: &[String]) -> Result<(Box<dyn LlmClient>, String), LlmError> {\n    let transport = Arc::new(UreqTransport::default());\n    let backend = args.first().map(String::as_str).unwrap_or(\"\");\n    let model = |i: usize, default: &str| args.get(i).cloned().unwrap_or_else(|| default.to_string());\n    match backend {\n        \"ollama\" => {\n            let Some(m) = args.get(1) else { usage() };\n            Ok((Box::new(OpenAiClient::ollama(transport)), m.clone()))\n        }\n        \"anthropic\" => Ok((Box::new(AnthropicClient::from_env()?), model(1, maluos_llm::anthropic::DEFAULT_MODEL))),\n        \"openai\" => Ok((Box::new(OpenAiClient::openai_from_env()?), model(1, maluos_llm::openai::DEFAULT_MODEL))),\n        \"compatible\" => {\n            let (Some(base), Some(m)) = (args.get(1), args.get(2)) else { usage() };\n            Ok((Box::new(OpenAiClient::compatible(transport, \"compatible\", base.clone(), None)), m.clone()))\n        }\n        _ => usage(),\n    }\n}\n\nfn run(client: &dyn LlmClient, model: &str) -> Result<(), LlmError> {\n    let tool = ToolDef {\n        name: \"slide_count\".into(),\n        description: \"Returns how many slides the open deck has.\".into(),\n        input_schema: serde_json::json!({\"type\": \"object\", \"properties\": {}, \"additionalProperties\": false}),\n    };\n    let system = \"You are the MaluOS Slides assistant. Use the slide_count tool when asked about the deck. Keep answers to one sentence.\";\n    let mut messages = vec![Message::user(\"How many slides does the open deck have?\")];\n    let mut out = std::io::stdout();\n\n    for turn in 1..=3 {\n        let request = Request::new(model, messages.clone()).with_system(system).with_tools(vec![tool.clone()]).with_max_tokens(400);\n        eprintln!(\"[{}] turn {turn}: {model}\", client.provider());\n        let completion = client.complete(&request, &mut |event| {\n            match event {\n                Event::TextDelta(t) => {\n                    let _ = out.write_all(t.as_bytes());\n                    let _ = out.flush();\n                }\n                Event::ThinkingDelta(t) => eprint!(\"\\x1b[2m{t}\\x1b[0m\"),\n                Event::ToolUseStart { name, id, .. } => eprintln!(\"\\n[tool use] {name} ({id})\"),\n                Event::ToolInputDelta { partial_json, .. } => eprint!(\"{partial_json}\"),\n                Event::Usage(u) => eprintln!(\"\\n[usage] in={} out={} cached={}\", u.input_tokens, u.output_tokens, u.cache_read_input_tokens),\n            }\n            Flow::Continue\n        })?;\n        println!();\n        eprintln!(\"[stop] {:?} ## 🤖 Claude

Ollama is installed and reachable, but the cloud model cannot run yet: the daemon is not signed in.

**What I found.** The daemon runs as a systemd service under the system user `ollama`, so it has its own key, separate from your user account. Your OAuth sign-in linked a different key, most likely the one belonging to whichever client you signed in from. Both checks agree:

- `ollama run glm-5.3-flash:cloud` answers "You need to be signed in to Ollama to run Cloud models."
- The crate's own live run against the daemon's OpenAI-compatible endpoint gets a 401 and reports it as a non-retryable `Auth` error, which is the correct mapping.

**What you need to do.** Open this link in a browser while logged in to ollama.com. It links the daemon's key to your account under the name `maluSlides-dev`.

```
https://ollama.com/connect?name=maluSlides-dev&key=c3NoLWVkMjU1MTkgQUFBQUMzTnphQzFsWkRJMU5URTVBQUFBSUJDSmVRY1k2Q2Exb3d0TGRMUjBJRDRHU3BMaERhM0F3S051UEdlNVlDU1A
```

If the page asks nothing more, the daemon is signed in at once with no restart needed. Then tell me and I will re-run the check.

**What I built meanwhile.** A live-check program now ships with the crate and is committed as `0858d3a8`. It sends one prompt with one tool, streams the reply, answers the tool call, and prints the stop reason and usage. Run it with:

```
cargo run -p maluos-llm --example live -- ollama glm-5.3-flash:cloud
```

The same program takes `anthropic`, `openai` or `compatible <base_url> <model>`, so it is the standing live test for every backend. Clippy, rustfmt and the docs are updated, and the Ollama state is recorded in the status file.

## 🤖 Claude

The check passes on both paths.

**Through `ollama run`.** The cloud model answered the prompt directly, so the daemon's key is linked and cloud access works from this machine.

**Through the crate.** The live example went through the daemon's OpenAI-compatible endpoint and completed a full two-turn exchange:

- Turn one streamed the model's reasoning as thinking deltas, then emitted a `slide_count` tool call and stopped with `ToolUse`.
- The example answered the tool call with "8", and turn two streamed the reply "The open deck has 8 slides." and stopped with `EndTurn`.
- Usage arrived on both turns, including the cached-token count, and the model name came back as `glm-5.3-flash`.

That is every part of the wire format the harness will depend on: request building, streaming, reasoning, tool use, tool results and usage. Step 3.1's "done when" is now met for the Ollama path. Anthropic and OpenAI stay mock-verified until a key is exported in the shell. The result is recorded in the status file and `llm.md`, committed as `bd0651c5` and pushed.

Next on the plan is step 3.3, the tool schema generated from the command catalog so MCP and the assistant share one table, then 3.2, the deck context builder. I will start when you say so.

//! MCP tool definitions (names, descriptions, JSON Schemas) and their implementations on top of a
//! [`Backend`].

use serde_json::{Value, json};

use crate::backend::Backend;
use crate::headless::NEEDS_APP;

/// The result of `tools/call`: MCP content blocks plus the `isError` flag.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct ToolResult {
    pub content: Vec<Value>,
    pub is_error: bool,
}

impl ToolResult {
    pub fn text(t: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self { content: vec![json!({"type": "text", "text": t.into()})], is_error: false }
    }
    pub fn json(v: &Value) -> Self {
        Self::text(serde_json::to_string_pretty(v).unwrap_or_default())
    }
    pub fn error(t: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self { content: vec![json!({"type": "text", "text": t.into()})], is_error: true }
    }
    pub fn image(png_base64: String, info: &Value) -> Self {
        Self {
            content: vec![json!({"type": "image", "data": png_base64, "mimeType": "image/png"}), json!({"type": "text", "text": info.to_string()})],
            is_error: false,
        }
    }
    pub fn to_value(&self) -> Value {
        json!({"content": self.content, "isError": self.is_error})
    }
}

fn num(desc: &str) -> Value {
    json!({"type": "number", "description": desc})
}
fn int(desc: &str) -> Value {
    json!({"type": "integer", "minimum": 0, "description": desc})
}
fn string(desc: &str) -> Value {
    json!({"type": "string", "description": desc})
}
fn boolean(desc: &str) -> Value {
    json!({"type": "boolean", "description": desc})
}
fn mods_schema() -> Value {
    json!({"type": "object", "additionalProperties": false, "description": "Modifier keys (cmd = Command on macOS / Ctrl elsewhere; alt = Option)", "properties": {"shift": {"type": "boolean"}, "alt": {"type": "boolean"}, "cmd": {"type": "boolean"}}})
}
fn obj(props: Value, required: &[&str]) -> Value {
    let mut o = json!({"type": "object", "properties": props, "additionalProperties": false});
    if !required.is_empty() {
        o["required"] = json!(required);
    }
    o
}
fn tool(name: &str, title: &str, desc: &str, schema: Value, read_only: bool) -> Value {
    json!({"name": name, "title": title, "description": desc, "inputSchema": schema, "annotations": {"title": title, "readOnlyHint": read_only, "openWorldHint": false}})
}

//! MaluOS Slides' MCP server.
//!
//! [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) over stdio: newline-delimited
//! JSON-RPC 2.0, hand-written (no async runtime). The server exposes MaluOS Slides as a set of MCP
//! tools and resources and forwards everything to a [`Backend`]:
//!
//! - [`Remote`] talks to a running desktop app through its loopback JSON-lines control channel
//!   (`maluos-slides --control 7979`): one `{"id","method","params"}` line in, one
//!   `{"id","ok","result"|"error"}` line out (see `docs/control-protocol.md`).
//! - [`Headless`] hosts an in-process [`maluos_slides_engine::Session`] and implements the
//!   engine-level control-channel methods itself (rendering pages with `maluos-slides-render`), so
//!   agents can build layouts and look at them without a window.
//!
//! Entry points: [`Server::serve`] (stdio loop) and [`Server::handle_line`] (one message).
#![deny(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::panic, clippy::unimplemented, clippy::todo, clippy::unreachable)]
#![forbid(unsafe_code)]

/// Default control-channel port of the desktop app.
pub const DEFAULT_PORT: u16 = 7979;

/// `"7979"` → `"127.0.0.1:7979"`; `"host:port"` is kept as is.
pub fn control_addr(s: &str) -> String {
    if s.parse::<u16>().is_ok() { format!("127.0.0.1:{s}") } else { s.to_string() }
}

//! Where MCP tool calls end up: a control-channel method call.

use std::io::{BufRead, BufReader, Read, Write};
use std::net::{TcpStream, ToSocketAddrs};
use std::time::Duration;

use serde_json::{Value, json};

// Includes the newline, matching the control server's request budget. In particular a peer
// must not be able to grow a reply indefinitely by withholding its newline.
const MAX_REPLY_BYTES: u64 = 16 * 1024 * 1024;

/// Something that answers control-channel methods (`engine.execute`, `document.inspect`,
/// `ui.pointer`, `ui.render`, …). See `maluos_slides_ui_egui::control` for the full list.
pub trait Backend {
    /// Call one method. `Ok` carries the `result`, `Err` the error message.
    fn call(&mut self, method: &str, params: Value) -> Result<Value, String>;
    /// True when a real UI is attached (`ui.screenshot`, `ui.click`, dialogs… work).
    fn has_ui(&self) -> bool;
    /// Short human description ("headless", "connected to 127.0.0.1:7979").
    fn describe(&self) -> String;
}

/// A running MaluOS Slides app, reached through its loopback control port.
pub struct Remote {
    addr: String,
    conn: Option<(BufReader<TcpStream>, TcpStream)>,
    next_id: u64,
}

impl Remote {
    /// Connect to `addr` (`127.0.0.1:7979`), failing fast when nothing is listening.
    pub fn connect(addr: &str) -> std::io::Result<Self> {
        let mut r = Self { addr: addr.to_string(), conn: None, next_id: 1 };
        r.reconnect()?;
        Ok(r)
    }

    pub fn addr(&self) -> &str {
        &self.addr
    }

    fn reconnect(&mut self) -> std::io::Result<()> {
        self.conn = None;
        let mut last = std::io::Error::new(std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound, format!("cannot resolve {}", self.addr));
        for sa in self.addr.to_socket_addrs()? {
            match TcpStream::connect_timeout(&sa, Duration::from_millis(800)) {
                Ok(s) => {
                    s.set_nodelay(true).ok();
                    // The app answers within 60 s (its own timeout); leave headroom.
                    s.set_read_timeout(Some(Duration::from_secs(90))).ok();
                    let read = s.try_clone()?;
                    self.conn = Some((BufReader::new(read), s));
                    return Ok(());
                }
                Err(e) => last = e,
            }
        }
        Err(last)
    }

//! Dependency layering rules (plan/architecture.md §3).
//!
//! The rule engine works on a small, metadata-independent model so it can be
//! unit-tested; `from_metadata` builds that model from `cargo metadata`.

use serde_json::Value;

/// Where a workspace crate sits.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Class {
    /// Regular layered crate.
    Layer(u8),
    /// Layer 0, and additionally may depend on no workspace crate at all.
    Standalone,
    /// Test tooling: may depend on anything up to L5 (it sits at L6 for rule
    /// purposes); other crates may use it only as a dev-dependency.
    Testkit,
    /// Binaries and build tooling: exempt from the rules.
    Exempt,
}

impl Class {
    fn layer(self) -> Option<u8> {
        match self {
            Class::Layer(l) => Some(l),
            Class::Standalone => Some(0),
            Class::Testkit => Some(6),
            Class::Exempt => None,
        }
    }
}

    ("render", Class::Layer(3)),

    ("pdf", Class::Layer(4)),
    ("engine", Class::Layer(5)),

/// Upward dev-dependencies allowed for integration tests: the PPTX round-trip tests drive the
/// engine (build a deck with commands, export, re-import).
pub const DEV_EXCEPTIONS: &[(&str, &str)] = &[("pptx", "engine")];

/// Explicit orderings *within* a layer (earlier may be used by later).
pub const INTRA_LAYER_ORDER: &[&[&str]] = &[];

fn intra_layer_allowed(from: &str, to: &str) -> bool {
    let (from, to) = (short_name(from), short_name(to));
    INTRA_LAYER_ORDER.iter().any(|chain| match (chain.iter().position(|n| *n == from), chain.iter().position(|n| *n == to)) {
        (Some(f), Some(t)) => t < f,
        _ => false,
    })
}

/// External crates that constitute a UI toolkit / windowing dependency.
/// Entries ending in `*` are prefixes.
pub const UI_CRATES: &[&str] = &["egui", "eframe", "winit", "egui_kittest", "rfd", "bevy*"];

/// First layer allowed to use UI crates.
pub const UI_MIN_LAYER: u8 = 6;

pub fn short_name(pkg: &str) -> &str {
    pkg.strip_prefix("maluos-slides-").unwrap_or(pkg)
}

pub fn classify(pkg: &str) -> Option<Class> {
    let s = short_name(pkg);
    TABLE.iter().find(|(n, _)| *n == s).map(|(_, c)| *c)
}

fn is_ui_crate(name: &str) -> bool {
    UI_CRATES.iter().any(|p| match p.strip_suffix('*') {
        Some(prefix) => name.starts_with(prefix),
        None => name == *p,
    })
}

pub fn parse_params(doc: &str) -> std::result::Result<Vec<Param<'_>>, String> {
    let doc = doc.split('→').next().unwrap_or_default();
    let mut params: Vec<Param> = vec![];
    let mut open: Vec<char> = vec![];
    let mut expect_key = false;
    let mut or = false;
    let mut objects: usize = 0;
    let mut about_from: Option<usize> = None;
    let mut chars = doc.char_indices().peekable();
    let mut prev = ' ';
    fn end_about<'a>(doc: &'a str, params: &mut [Param<'a>], from: &mut Option<usize>, to: usize) {
        if let (Some(f), Some(p)) = (from.take(), params.last_mut()) {
            p.about = doc.get(f..to).unwrap_or_default().trim();
        }
    }
    while let Some((i, c)) = chars.next() {
        let in_object = open == ['{'];
        match c {
            '{' | '[' | '(' => {
                open.push(c);
                if open == ['{'] {
                    expect_key = true;
                    objects += 1;
                    or = false;
                }
            }
            '}' | ']' | ')' => {
                if in_object {
                    end_about(doc, &mut params, &mut about_from, i);
                }
                open.pop();
            }
            ',' if in_object => {
                end_about(doc, &mut params, &mut about_from, i);
                expect_key = true;
            }
            '|' if in_object && prev == ' ' && chars.peek().is_some_and(|(_, n)| *n == ' ') => {
                end_about(doc, &mut params, &mut about_from, i);
                expect_key = true;
                or = true;
            }
            c if in_object && expect_key && (c.is_ascii_alphabetic() || c == '_') => {
                let mut end = i + c.len_utf8();
                while let Some((j, n)) = chars.peek().copied().filter(|(_, n)| n.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || *n == '_') {
                    end = j + n.len_utf8();
                    chars.next();
                }
                let after = doc.get(end..).unwrap_or_default();
                let rest = after.trim_start_matches('?').trim_start();
                let at = doc.len() - rest.len();
                about_from = match rest.chars().next() {
                    Some(':') => Some(at + 1),
                    Some('(') => Some(at),
                    Some(',' | '}' | '|') => None,

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct HistoryEntry {
    pub label: String,
    pub doc: Arc<Presentation>,
    pub selection: Selection,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub struct History {
    pub undo: Vec<HistoryEntry>,
    pub redo: Vec<HistoryEntry>,
    pub limit: usize,
    /// Most memory (estimated bytes) the undo steps may keep beyond the current document;
    /// 0 means [`UNDO_BYTE_BUDGET`].
    pub byte_limit: usize,
    /// Estimated bytes each undo step keeps that the document after it doesn't share, by the
    /// step's document address.
    pub costs: std::collections::HashMap<usize, usize>,
}

pub(crate) fn push_undo(st: &mut DocState, e: HistoryEntry) {
    let h = &mut st.history;
    h.costs.insert(Arc::as_ptr(&e.doc) as usize, undo_cost(&e.doc, &st.doc));
    h.undo.push(e);
    h.redo.clear();
    if h.undo.len() > h.limit.max(1) {
        h.undo.remove(0);
    }
    // Memory too: drop the oldest steps while the kept ones pass the budget (the newest always
    // stays, however big). A deck-wide edit keeps a copy of every slide, so 500 of them on a big
    // deck could hold hundreds of copies.
    let budget = if h.byte_limit == 0 { UNDO_BYTE_BUDGET } else { h.byte_limit };
    let cost = |h: &History, e: &HistoryEntry| h.costs.get(&(Arc::as_ptr(&e.doc) as usize)).copied().unwrap_or(0);
    let mut total: usize = h.undo.iter().map(|e| cost(h, e)).sum();
    let mut drop = 0;
    while total > budget && drop + 1 < h.undo.len() {
        total -= cost(h, &h.undo[drop]);
        drop += 1;
    }
    if drop > 0 {
        h.undo.drain(..drop);
    }
    // Costs of steps that are gone (dropped, or redo steps cleared above).
    if h.costs.len() > h.undo.len() + 16 {
        let live: std::collections::HashSet<usize> = h.undo.iter().chain(h.redo.iter()).map(|e| Arc::as_ptr(&e.doc) as usize).collect();
        h.costs.retain(|k, _| live.contains(k));
    }
}

        let spec = find_command(id).ok_or_else(|| EngineError::UnknownCommand(id.into()))?;
        // Any other edit (or a click, a key, undo) settles an input method's composition first.

    pub fn info(&self, s: &Session) -> CommandInfo {

pub fn always(_: &Session) -> std::result::Result<(), String> {
    Ok(())
}
pub fn has_doc(s: &Session) -> std::result::Result<(), String> {
    s.active().map(|_| ()).ok_or_else(|| "no presentation open".into())
}
pub fn has_slide(s: &Session) -> std::result::Result<(), String> {
    has_doc(s)?;
    if s.active().is_some_and(|d| !d.doc.slides.is_empty() || d.selection.target != crate::Target::Slides) { Ok(()) } else { Err("no slides".into()) }
}
pub const NOTHING_SELECTED: &str = "nothing selected";
pub const SELECT_TWO: &str = "select two or more objects";
pub const NO_TEXT_POINT: &str = "no text insertion point";
pub const SELECT_TEXT_OR_SHAPE: &str = "select text or a shape";
pub fn has_selection(s: &Session) -> std::result::Result<(), String> {
    has_doc(s)?;
    if s.active().is_some_and(|d| !d.selection.shapes.is_empty()) { Ok(()) } else { Err(NOTHING_SELECTED.into()) }
}
pub fn has_two(s: &Session) -> std::result::Result<(), String> {
    has_doc(s)?;
    if s.active().is_some_and(|d| d.selection.shapes.len() >= 2) { Ok(()) } else { Err(SELECT_TWO.into()) }
}
pub fn has_text(s: &Session) -> std::result::Result<(), String> {
    has_doc(s)?;
    if s.active().is_some_and(|d| d.selection.text.is_some()) { Ok(()) } else { Err(NO_TEXT_POINT.into()) }
}
/// Text editing or selected shapes (formatting commands apply to either).
pub fn has_text_or_shapes(s: &Session) -> std::result::Result<(), String> {
    has_doc(s)?;
    if s.active().is_some_and(|d| d.selection.text.is_some() || !d.selection.shapes.is_empty()) { Ok(()) } else { Err(SELECT_TEXT_OR_SHAPE.into()) }
}

pub fn can_undo(s: &Session) -> std::result::Result<(), String> {
    if s.active().is_some_and(|d| !d.history.undo.is_empty()) { Ok(()) } else { Err("nothing to undo".into()) }
}
pub fn can_redo(s: &Session) -> std::result::Result<(), String> {
    if s.active().is_some_and(|d| !d.history.redo.is_empty()) { Ok(()) } else { Err("nothing to redo".into()) }
}

macro_rules! cmd {
    ($id:literal, $label:literal, [$($m:literal),*], $sc:expr, $params:literal, $en:expr, $run:expr) => {
        $crate::cmd::CommandSpec { id: $id, label: $label, menu: &[$($m),*], shortcut: $sc, params: $params, enabled: $en, run: $run, journal: true, undoable: true }
    };
    (query $id:literal, $label:literal, [$($m:literal),*], $sc:expr, $params:literal, $en:expr, $run:expr) => {
        $crate::cmd::CommandSpec { id: $id, label: $label, menu: &[$($m),*], shortcut: $sc, params: $params, enabled: $en, run: $run, journal: false, undoable: false }
    };
    (noundo $id:literal, $label:literal, [$($m:literal),*], $sc:expr, $params:literal, $en:expr, $run:expr) => {
        $crate::cmd::CommandSpec { id: $id, label: $label, menu: &[$($m),*], shortcut: $sc, params: $params, enabled: $en, run: $run, journal: true, undoable: false }
    };
}

## 🤖 Claude

Phase 3.3 is done, committed as `d3ff0563` and pushed to `origin main`.

**What landed.** A new fork crate, `crates/maluos-slides-assist`, that gives the assistant the same view of the application the MCP server has. No upstream crate was edited.

- **One table.** The tool list a model sees is built straight from the MCP server's definitions, converted to the `maluos-llm` tool type. A headless session drops the two tools that need a window, so the model is never offered a call that cannot succeed. The server's read-only hints come along for the safety rails in step 3.5.
- **Generated command schemas.** Every engine command's parameter doc is parsed with the engine's own grammar and turned into a JSON Schema: property names, descriptions, the required keys, a type where the doc leaves no doubt. All 300-plus docs parse, and a test guards that against upstream drift.
- **Validation before action.** A `run_command` call is checked before it runs. An unknown command gets a "did you mean" suggestion within two edits. An undocumented key is refused with the documented keys in the message, so a misspelled parameter never silently takes the default. A batch is checked whole first, so a bad second command leaves the first unrun.
- **Execution through the engine.** One tool call goes through an MCP backend, headless or a running app, and comes back shaped as the tool-result block the next model request carries. Results are capped at 64 KiB with a marker. Rendered images are kept aside until image inputs arrive in Phase 4.
- **Snapshots.** The tool table and the full catalog with schemas are checked in under the crate's `snapshots` folder. An upstream merge that adds or re-documents a command shows up as a readable diff.

**Verification.** 12 new tests and the MCP crate's 25 tests pass. Clippy, rustfmt, the layering check (30 crates), the wasm32 check and the asset check are all green. The crate is described in `docs/maluos-slides/assistant.md`, and the status file records the step.

**One design note.** The engine pushes one undo entry per command and has no grouping call. Rather than edit the engine, the loop in step 3.4 will fold the entries a turn added into one, since the history is public. That keeps the "one undo step per turn" rule without touching upstream code.

Next is step 3.2, the deck context builder, then 3.4, the loop. I will start when you say so.

//! Inspection for agents: the deck, slides and shapes as JSON (verify work without screenshots).

use maluos_slides_model::resolve::{self, Ctx};
use maluos_slides_model::{Shape, ShapeKind};
use serde_json::{Value, json};

use super::*;
use crate::{Result, Session};

pub fn specs() -> Vec<CommandSpec> {
    vec![
        cmd!(query "document.inspect", "Inspect Presentation", [], None, "{} → slides with titles, layouts, shape counts; selection; size; theme", has_doc, document),
        cmd!(query "slide.inspect", "Inspect Slide", [], None, "{index?} → the slide's shapes with ids, kinds, boxes, text, fills, animations, transition, notes (text, and notesBody with its formatting)", has_doc, slide),
        cmd!(query "shape.inspect", "Inspect Shape", [], None, "{id} → full shape JSON plus its effective box", has_doc, shape),
        cmd!(query "commands.list", "List Commands", [], None, "{filter?: substring} → [{id, label, params, enabled}]", always, commands),
    ]
}

fn document(s: &mut Session, _p: &Value) -> Result<Value> {
    let st = s.doc()?;
    let d = &st.doc;
    let slides: Vec<Value> = d
        .slides
        .iter()
        .enumerate()
        .map(|(i, sl)| {
            let layout = d.layout(sl.layout).map(|(_, l)| l.name.clone()).unwrap_or_default();
            json!({"index": i, "id": sl.id, "title": sl.title(), "layout": layout, "shapes": sl.shapes.len(), "hidden": sl.hidden, "transition": sl.transition.as_ref().map(|t| t.kind.clone()), "animations": sl.animations.len(), "notes": sl.notes_text()})
        })
        .collect();
    let m = d.masters.first();
    Ok(json!({
        "title": st.title(),
        "path": st.path,
        "dirty": st.is_dirty(),
        "slideSize": [d.slide_size.width, d.slide_size.height],
        "slides": slides,
        "sections": d.sections.iter().map(|x| json!({"name": x.name, "slides": x.slides.len()})).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
        "theme": m.map(|m| m.theme.name.clone()),
        "fonts": m.map(|m| json!({"major": m.theme.fonts.major.latin, "minor": m.theme.fonts.minor.latin})),
        "layouts": m.map(|m| m.layouts.iter().map(|l| json!({"id": l.id, "name": l.name})).collect::<Vec<_>>()),
        "selection": serde_json::to_value(&st.selection).unwrap_or_default(),
        "media": d.media.iter().map(|x| json!({"id": x.id, "name": x.name, "type": x.content_type, "bytes": x.data.len()})).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
        "undo": st.history.undo.last().map(|e| e.label.clone()),
        "redo": st.history.redo.last().map(|e| e.label.clone()),
    }))
}

    let x = ctx.map(|c| resolve::xfrm(c, sh)).or(sh.xfrm).unwrap_or_default();

            Some(maluos_slides_model::Fill::Solid { color }) => json!(format!("#{}", c.color(&color, ph).hex())),

        "rotation": x.rot,

            o.insert("placeholder".into(), json!(p.kind.xml()));

        }
        if let Some(f) = fill {
            o.insert("fill".into(), f);
        }
        if sh.hidden {

\"{} slides, {}×{} pt, theme {}{}{}\",\n            d.slides.len(),\n            d.slide_size.width,\n            d.slide_size.height,\n            theme_line(d),\n            if st.is_dirty() { \", A header: title and path, slide count, slide size, the theme with its heading and body fonts\n   and the dark, light and six accent colours as hex, unsaved-changes flag, section count.\n2. The selection: current slide, selected slides, the text being edited (shape, cell, caret or\n   range with the selected text quoted), selected table cells, and every selected shape as one\n   line (`ctrTitle placeholder id 258 \"Title 1\" at [120,88,720,188] text \"…\"`), named as the\n   target of an edit.\n3. The current slide, whole: title line with layout, id, hidden flag, animation count and\n   transition; each text placeholder as `[obj id 263]` followed by its paragraphs as indented\n   bullets (outline levels kept, so the model can rewrite one line); every other shape as one\n   line from `shape_summary` (preset or kind, id, name, box, rotation, fill, table size and first\n   rows, chart type and series count, group size, text, alt text); notes.\n4. The outline: every slide the same way, with `### Section: name` headings where sections\n   start, and the current slide as a one-line pointer.\n\n`Budget` (default 24 KiB total, 1200 bytes per slide, 400 chars per shape text, 4000 on the\ncurrent slide, 300 for notes) is enforced slide by slide with markers the model can act on:\n`… more shapes [cut: inspect_slide 7]`, `[body left out: inspect_slide 40]` once the total is\nreached, and `… N more slides (inspect_document lists them)` past a margin. `Context::cut_slides`\nlists what was cut. The current slide is written first and is never cut by the total.\n\n`ContextCache::get` returns the last outline unless the document uid, its revision or the\nselection changed, so a pane polling every frame builds nothing between edits.\n\n## Snapshots\n'''\nassert old in s; s=s.replace(old,new,1)\ns=s.replace(\"`snapshots/tools.json` is the tool table (every tool, app-only included) and\\n`snapshots/commands.json` the catalog with each command's generated schema.\",\n            \"`snapshots/tools.json` is the tool table (every tool, app-only included),\\n`snapshots/commands.json` the catalog with each command's generated schema, and\\n`snapshots/context-sample.md` the outline of the sample deck (`engine::sample`) on slide 2.\")\ns=s.replace(\"`cargo nextest run -p maluos-slides-assist`: 12 tests.\", \"`cargo nextest run -p maluos-slides-assist`: 17 tests.\")\ns=s.replace(\"long-result shaping. ## 🤖 Claude

Phase 3.2 is done, committed as `63bdac86` and pushed to `origin main`.

**What landed.** A context module in the assistant crate that writes the open deck as prompt text, read straight from the engine state. Reading is free; only edits go through commands.

- **Header.** Title and path, slide count and size, the theme with its heading and body fonts and the dark, light and six accent colours as hex, an unsaved-changes flag, the section count.
- **Selection.** The current slide, selected slides, the text being edited with its caret or range and the selected text quoted, selected table cells, and each selected shape on one line, named as the target of an edit. That is the "selection is the target" rule from your vision made concrete.
- **Current slide, whole.** Each text placeholder is shown with its id and its paragraphs as indented bullets with outline levels kept, so the model can rewrite one line. Every other shape is one summary line: preset, id, name, box, fill, table size and first rows, chart type and series count, text, alt text. Notes follow.
- **Outline.** Every other slide the same way, with section headings where sections start.
- **Budget with markers.** Default 24 KiB total and 1200 bytes per slide. When a slide overflows, the model sees "more shapes, inspect_slide 7". Past the total, slides keep only their title with a "body left out" marker. Past a margin, a single count remains. The current slide is written first and is never cut by the total.
- **Cache.** Keyed on document id, revision and selection, so a pane polling every frame rebuilds nothing between edits.

**Verification.** 17 tests in the crate and 25 in the MCP crate pass. Clippy, rustfmt, the layering check and doctests are green. The sample-deck outline is checked in as a snapshot and reads well: sections, titles, the agenda slide's bullets, the chart and the shape diagram on slide 4 all appear in a form a model can edit against.

Next is step 3.4, the loop: message, prompt, model, tool calls through the engine, one undo step per turn, limits on turns and tokens, tested headless with the mock backend. I will start when you say so.

args.get(1), args.get(2)) else { usage() };\n    let flag = |name: &str| args.iter().position(|a| a == name).and_then(|i| args.get(i + 1)).cloned();\n    let open = flag(\"--open\");\n    let save = flag(\"--save\");\n    let sample = args.iter().any(|a| a == \"--sample\");\n\n    let transport = Arc::new(UreqTransport::default());\n    let (client, model): (Arc<dyn LlmClient>, String) = match backend.as_str() {\n        \"ollama\" => (Arc::new(OpenAiClient::ollama(transport)), model.clone()),\n        \"anthropic\" => match AnthropicClient::from_env() {\n            Ok(c) => (Arc::new(c), if model.is_empty() { maluos_llm::anthropic::DEFAULT_MODEL.into() } else { model.clone() }),\n            Err(e) => {\n                eprintln!(\"error: {e}\");\n                std::process::exit(1)\n            }\n        },\n        \"openai\" => match OpenAiClient::openai_from_env() {\n            Ok(c) => (Arc::new(c), if model.is_empty() { maluos_llm::openai::DEFAULT_MODEL.into() } else { model.clone() }),\n            Err(e) => {\n                eprintln!(\"error: {e}\");\n                std::process::exit(1)\n            }\n        },\n        _ => usage(),\n    };\n\n    let mut host = Headless::new();\n    let opened = if let Some(p) = &open {\n        host.session.execute(\"file.open\", &json!({\"path\": p}))\n    } else if sample {\n        maluos_slides_engine::sample::open_sample(&mut host.session).map(|_| json!({}))\n    } else {\n        host.session.execute(\"file.new\", &json!({}))\n    };\n    if let Err(e) = opened {\n        eprintln!(\"error: {e}\");\n        std::process::exit(1)\n    }\n\n    let mut assistant = Assistant::new(client, model);\n    let mut out = std::io::stdout();\n    let report = assistant.ask(&mut host, request, &mut |e| {\n        match e {\n            TurnEvent::Round(n) => eprintln!(\"\\x1b[2m[round {n}]\\x1b[0m\"),\n            TurnEvent::Text(t) => {\n                let _ = out.write_all(t.as_bytes());\n                let _ = out.flush();\n            }\n            TurnEvent::Thinking(t) => eprint!(\"\\x1b[2m{t}\\x1b[0m\"),\n            TurnEvent::ToolStart { name, input } => eprintln!(\"\\x1b[36m[tool] {name} {input}\\x1b[0m\"),\n            TurnEvent::ToolDone(o) => {\n                let first = o.text.lines().next().unwrap_or(\"\");\n                eprintln!(\"\\x1b[2m[{}] {}{}\\x1b[0m\", if o.is_error { \"error\" } else { \"ok\" }, &first[..first.len().min(200)], if o.text.len() > 200 { \"…\" } else { \"\" });\n            }\n        }\n        Flow::Continue\n    });\n    println!();\n    eprintln!(\"[turn] rounds={} tool calls={} commands={:?} tokens in={} out={} undo={:?} stopped={:?} error={:?}\", report.rounds, report.tool_calls.len(), report.commands, report.usage.input_tokens, report.usage.output_tokens, report.undo_label, report.stopped, report.error);\n    if let Some(p) = save {\n        match host.session.execute(\"file.save\", &json!({\"path\": p})) {\n            Ok(_) => eprintln!(\"[saved] {p}\"),\n            Err(e) => eprintln!(\"[save failed] {e}\"),\n        }\n    }\n    if report.error.is_some() {\n        std::process::exit(1)\n    }\n}\nEOF\nexport CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=6; systemd-run --user --scope -q -p MemoryHigh=4500M -p MemoryMax=6G cargo clippy -p ## 🤖 Claude

Phase 3.4 is done, committed as `acb6a827` and pushed to `origin main`.

**What landed.** The loop, in the assistant crate. One user message goes in, tool calls run through the engine, one answer comes out, and the whole turn is one undo step.

- **Prompt.** Standing instructions, the command catalog listing, and the deck outline, rebuilt every round so the model sees its own edits as it works. The conversation persists across turns and is trimmed at user messages, so a tool call never loses its result.
- **Tools through the engine.** Every call runs through the validated tool path from step 3.3, so through `Session::execute`. The pane gets round, text, thinking, tool-start and tool-done events, and can cancel from the callback.
- **One undo step per turn.** The engine pushes one history entry per command and has no grouping call. The loop records the document pointer before the turn and afterwards folds everything the turn pushed into one entry labelled with the request. No upstream crate was edited.
- **Limits and errors.** Twelve rounds, forty tool calls and 8k output tokens per turn by default. Past the tool-call limit, calls are answered with an error telling the model to finish. Rate limits, overloads and transport failures are retried with backoff. Other errors end the turn with the user's message kept, so they can retry without retyping. A cancelled or failed turn closes any dangling tool call, so the next request is still valid.

**Verification.** The plan's own test passes with the mock backend: "add a closing slide that thanks the audience" produces `slide.new` then `set_text`, the slide and its text exist, the journal shows exactly those two commands, and the history holds one entry that a single undo reverts whole. 25 tests in the crate, 66 across the three new crates. Clippy, rustfmt, layering and doctests are green.

**Live run.** A new example runs one turn against a real model. Against the Ollama cloud model on the sample deck it took three rounds, inserted a "Thank you!" title slide at the end with a subtitle, inspected the deck, and saved a correct 9-slide `.pptx` with one undo step. One flaw showed up: on round two the model saw its own new slide in the rebuilt outline and took it for pre-existing content. The instructions now state that the outline already includes the turn's edits. Input cost was about 39k tokens for the turn, mostly the catalog, which prompt caching will cut later.

Next is step 3.5, the safety rails: answer-only, confirm-before-change and autopilot modes, with destructive commands always confirmed. I will start when you say so.

Safety rails: what the assistant may do on its own, what it must ask about, what it may not.\n//!\n//! Three modes (owner decision D11, step 3.5):\n//! - **answer only**: nothing changes; the model reads and explains.\n//! - **confirm**: every change is shown as a plan (the tool calls and the engine commands behind\n//!   them) and applied only when the user approves it.\n//! - **autopilot**: changes apply at once; destructive commands (deleting slides or sections,\n//!   starting or opening another presentation, clearing a deck's content) are still confirmed.\n\nuse serde_json::Value;\n\nuse crate::catalog::Catalog;\nuse crate::tools::ToolTable;\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]\npub enum Mode {\n    AnswerOnly,\n    #[default]\n    Confirm,\n    Autopilot,\n}\n\nimpl Mode {\n    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {\n        match self {\n            Mode::AnswerOnly => \"answer-only\",\n            Mode::Confirm => \"confirm\",\n            Mode::Autopilot => \"autopilot\",\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn parse(s: &str) -> Option<Mode> {\n        Some(match s.trim().to_ascii_lowercase().as_str() {\n            \"answer\" | \"answer-only\" | \"answeronly\" | \"ask\" | \"read\" => Mode::AnswerOnly,\n            \"confirm\" | \"review\" => Mode::Confirm,\n            \"autopilot\" | \"auto\" | \"apply\" => Mode::Autopilot,\n            _ => return None,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// One line for the system text.\n    pub fn instruction(self) -> &'static str {\n        match self {\n            Mode::AnswerOnly => \"Mode: answer only. You cannot change the presentation in this mode: inspect it and say what you would do and which commands you would run. run_command accepts only query commands (inspect, describe, list).\",\n            Mode::Confirm => \"Mode: confirm. Every change you make is shown to the user as a plan and applied only when they approve it. Group the calls of one change together. If the user declines a plan, do not retry it; ask what they want instead.\",\n            Mode::Autopilot => \"Mode: autopilot. Your changes apply at once; destructive ones (deleting slides or sections, replacing the presentation) are confirmed by the user first. If the user declines one, do not retry it.\",\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Commands that destroy content or replace the presentation: confirmed in every mode that\n/// allows changes.\npub const DESTRUCTIVE_COMMANDS: &[&str] = &[\n    \"slide.delete\",\n    \"section.remove\",\n    \"section.removeAll\",\n    \"master.deleteLayout\",\n    \"file.new\",\n    \"file.open\",\n    \"file.openBytes\",\n    \"file.close\",\n    \"file.revert\",\n    \"file.adopt\",\n    \"file.recovery.open\",\n];\n\n/// Tools that run a destructive command.\npub const DESTRUCTIVE_TOOLS: &[&str] = &[\"new_presentation\", \"open_presentation\"];\n\n/// What a tool call does, in the policy's eyes.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord)]\npub enum Class {\n    ReadOnly,\n    Change,\n    Destructive,\n}\n\n/// What to do with one call.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum Decision {\n    Allow,\n    /// Ask the user first.\n    Confirm,\n    /// Do not run; the model gets this reason.\n    Refuse(String),\n}\n\n/// One tool call as the user sees it before approving.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]\npub struct PlannedCall {\n    pub tool_use_id: String,\n    pub name: String,\n    pub input: Value,\n    pub class: Class,\n    /// The engine commands behind it: (id, label, params). For `run_command` and `batch` the\n    /// real ones; for the other tools the command the MCP server maps them to.\n    pub commands: Vec<(String, String, Value)>,\n}\n\nimpl PlannedCall {\n    /// A few lines for a dialog or the terminal.\n    pub fn describe(&self) -> String {\n        let mut s = String::new();\n        s.push_str(&self.name);\n        if self.class == Class::Destructive {\n            s.push_str(\" (destructive)\");\n        }\n        match self.name.as_str() {\n            \"run_command\" | \"batch\" => {\n                for (id, label, params) in &self.commands {\n                    let p = if params.is_null() || params == &Value::Object(Default::default()) { String::new() } else { format!(\" {params}\") };\n                    s.push_str(&format!(\"\\n  {id} — {label}{p}\"));\n                }\n            }\n            _ => {\n                if let Some(o) = self.input.as_object().filter(|o| !o.is_empty()) {\n                    let args: Vec<String> = o.iter().map(|(k, v)| format!(\"{k}={}\", short(v))).collect();\n                    s.push_str(&format!(\" {}\", args.join(\" \")));\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        s\n    }\n}\n\n/// The calls of one round that need the user's approval, shown together.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]\npub struct Plan {\n    pub calls: Vec<PlannedCall>,\n}\n\nimpl Plan {\n    pub fn destructive(&self) -> bool {\n        self.calls.iter().any(|c| c.class == Class::Destructive)\n    }\n\n    pub fn describe(&self) -> String {\n        self.calls.iter().map(PlannedCall::describe).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(\"\\n\")\n    }\n}\n\n/// The user's answer to a plan.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum Verdict {\n    Approve,\n    /// Not this; the reason, if any, goes to the model.\n    Decline(Option<String>),\n    /// Stop the whole turn.\n    Cancel,\n}\n\n/// Who answers a plan: a dialog, a terminal prompt, a test.\npub trait Confirm {\n    fn confirm(&mut self, plan: &Plan) -> Verdict;\n}\n\nimpl<F: FnMut(&Plan) -> Verdict> Confirm for F {\n    fn confirm(&mut self, plan: &Plan) -> Verdict {\n        self(plan)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Approves everything: scripts, tests, the CLI with `--yes`.\npub struct ApproveAll;\n\nimpl Confirm for ApproveAll {\n    fn confirm(&mut self, _: &Plan) -> Verdict {\n        Verdict::Approve\n    }\n}\n\n/// Declines everything: answer-only behaviour for a host without a dialog.\npub struct DeclineAll;\n\nimpl Confirm for DeclineAll {\n    fn confirm(&mut self, _: &Plan) -> Verdict {\n        Verdict::Decline(Some(\"no one is there to approve changes\".into()))\n    }\n}\n\n/// The rails for one mode.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct Policy {\n    pub mode: Mode,\n    pub destructive_commands: Vec<String>,\n    pub destructive_tools: Vec<String>,\n}\n\nimpl Policy {\n    pub fn new(mode: Mode) -> Self {\n        Policy {\n            mode,\n            destructive_commands: DESTRUCTIVE_COMMANDS.iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect(),\n            destructive_tools: DESTRUCTIVE_TOOLS.iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn is_destructive_command(&self, id: &str) -> bool {\n        self.destructive_commands.iter().any(|c| c == id)\n    }\n\n    /// The tools the model is offered in this mode: everything, call does and the commands behind it.\n    pub fn classify(&self, table: &ToolTable, catalog: &Catalog, tool_use_id: &str, name: &str, input: &Value) -> PlannedCall {\n        let mut commands = Vec::new();\n        let mut class = if table.is_read_only(name) { Class::ReadOnly } else { Class::Change };\n        let mut note = |id: &str, params: Value, class: &mut Class| {\n            let (label, query) = catalog.get(id).map(|e| (e.label.to_string(), e.is_query())).unwrap_or_else(|| (String::new(), false));\n            let c = if self.is_destructive_command(id) {\n                Class::Destructive\n            } else if query {\n                Class::ReadOnly\n            } else {\n                Class::Change\n            };\n            *class = (*class).max(c);\n #[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use serde_json::json;

    use crate::Session;

    #[test]
    fn invalid_index_params_are_rejected_not_defaulted_to_selection() {
        let mut s = Session::with_new();
        while s.doc().expect("doc").doc.slides.len() < 3 {
            s.execute("slide.new", &json!({})).expect("new slide");
        }
        for bad in [json!(-1), json!(1.5)] {
            for (cmd, p) in [
                ("slide.delete", json!({"index": bad})),
                ("slide.duplicate", json!({"index": bad})),
                ("slide.move", json!({"from": bad, "to": 0})),
                ("section.add", json!({"at": bad})),
            ] {
                assert!(s.execute(cmd, &p).is_err(), "{cmd} must reject {p}");
                assert_eq!(s.doc().expect("doc").doc.slides.len(), 3, "{cmd} {p}");
            }
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn duplicate_keeps_section_order_in_step_with_slides() {
        let mut s = Session::with_new();
        while s.doc().expect("doc").doc.slides.len() < 3 {
            s.execute("slide.new", &json!({})).expect("new slide");
        }
        s.execute("section.add", &json!({"at": 0})).expect("section");
        let orig = s.doc().expect("doc").doc.slides.first().expect("slide").id;
        s.execute("slide.duplicate", &json!({"index": 0})).expect("dup");
        let st = s.doc().expect("doc");
        let all: Vec<_> = st.doc.slides.iter().map(|x| x.id).collect();
        let sec = &st.doc.sections.first().expect("section").slides;
        assert_eq!(all.len(), 4);
        assert_eq!(sec, &all, "section order must match slide order");
        assert_eq!(sec.first(), Some(&orig));
    }

ok
```

## 🤖 Claude

Phase 3.5 is done. Two commits are pushed: `7cecfc38` with the rails and `79d82c13` with a small engine fix the live run exposed.

**What landed.** A policy module in the assistant crate with three modes.

- **Answer-only.** The model is offered only reading tools, plus `run_command` for query commands. Any change is refused with a reason the model reads, so it explains what it would do instead.
- **Confirm, the default.** Every change is shown to you as a plan before it runs. A plan lists each tool call with its arguments and the engine commands behind it, with their labels. You approve, decline with a reason the model hears, or cancel the turn. One plan per round, read-only calls run without asking.
- **Autopilot.** Changes apply at once. Destructive commands are still confirmed: deleting slides, sections or layouts, and starting, opening, closing or reverting a presentation. A batch is as dangerous as its worst command, and the whole batch is shown. The report lists the slides the turn added or changed and how many it removed, so the answer can say where to look.

The confirmation is a small trait, so the pane in step 3.6 can block on a dialog while the CLI prompts on the terminal. The example program now takes a mode flag and prompts for plans.

**Verification.** Six new tests cover the destructive lists against the real catalog, classification and decisions per mode, plan text, and each mode end to end through the mock model. 31 tests in the crate, 72 across the three new crates. Clippy, rustfmt and layering are green.

**Live run and an engine fix.** Against the Ollama cloud model in autopilot, "delete the last slide" produced two destructive plans, each shown and flagged correctly. The model deleted by index, then tried again with the id it had just deleted. The engine accepted that stale id as a silent success with an undo step and a journal line. That is an upstream bug, so I fixed it in the engine with a test: `slide.delete` now drops ids the deck lacks and fails when none is left. The fix is the kind the project rules allow in upstream crates, and it is worth sending upstream.

Next is step 3.6, the assistant pane in the desktop app: a right-hand pane with the conversation, streaming answer, the commands it ran with Undo per turn, mode selector, model picker and provider status, plus an "Ask Malu" ribbon button and Ctrl+Shift+A. That step touches `crates/ui-egui` through fenced hooks and needs the headless GUI check, which requires `xvfb` installed with sudo. I will start when you say so.
