maluctl office: this desk and its office (Phase 12 slice 6, docs/desk-enrolment.md).

A MaluOS desktop joins a Business OS office as a *desk*: a location in the
office's estate that belongs to the person at the keyboard. Enrolment
exchanges a one-time code the office gave the person for a desk token; the
token lives in the person's vault compartment (office-desk-token), never in
a file. The office's model endpoint becomes a rung of this desk's gateway
(--model office) applied with that token on the person's behalf, and the
session heartbeats the office while the person is signed in, so the estate
shows the desk and whether it is online.

  sudo maluctl office enroll URL --code CODE [--name "Ed's desk"] [--owner LOGIN] [--no-gateway] [--force]
  maluctl office status [--json] [--live]          the configuration and the last heartbeat; --live asks the office
  maluctl office heartbeat [--presence online|offline] [--json]       as the desk's owner
  maluctl office apps [--json] [--refresh]         the MaluApps catalogue: the office's (endpoints.apps) over the
                                                   public one (download.maluos.com/apps/catalog.json, signed by the
                                                   MaluOS release key: catalog.json.asc, verified with the archive
                                                   keyring; refused unsigned), cached per user
  maluctl office apps install|remove|open ID       a web app becomes a launcher opening it in Firefox's own window;
                                                   a deb app installs from apt.maluos.com (pkexec apt-get)
  maluctl office agents [--json] [--refresh]       the office's agents this desk may use (endpoints.agents; Phase 12 slice 8)
  maluctl office agent ID card|activity|tasks [--json]       one of them: its card, its recent activity, the tasks sent from here
  maluctl office agent ID send TEXT [--json]       give it a task and wait for the answer (its task URL, the desk token)
  sudo maluctl office leave [--keep-secret]

Agents: /etc/maluos/office.env names the office's endpoints (MALUOS_OFFICE_*)
for every maluos-agent@ unit. The owner lets an agent use the office's
models with `maluctl secret delegate --to agent:NAME --secret office-desk-token`
and read the token for the office's MCP servers with
`maluctl secret grant office-desk-token --to agent:NAME --level read`.

---
maluctl agent: an agent as a system concept.

One command creates everything an agent needs on a MaluOS host, and one
removes it: a Linux system user, a MaluDB principal with scope grants, the
identity mapping for the vault and the gateway, its own vault compartment,
a gateway policy (class, tiers, cloud, egress ceiling, budget), optionally
a gateway token, and a hardened systemd unit (maluos-agent@NAME) that runs
the agent's command as that user with the MaluOS endpoints in its
environment.

  maluctl agent create NAME [--exec CMD] [--name "Display"] [--home SCOPE] [--scope SCOPE:read|write ...]
                     [--class agent] [--tiers a,b] [--backends a,b] [--cloud yes|no] [--egress public|internal|restricted]
                     [--budget usd_per_day=1] [--token] [--sandbox standard|strict] [--no-start]
                     [--owner user:NAME | --owner none]   who the agent belongs to (default: the sudo user)
  maluctl agent list [--json] | show NAME
  maluctl agent start|stop|restart|status|logs NAME
  maluctl agent run NAME -- CMD...            run a command as the agent (its identity, its environment)
  maluctl agent card NAME [--json]            what the agent says about itself (its task interface, Phase 12 slice 8)
  maluctl agent send NAME TEXT [--json]

"""maluos_agent_tasks: the task interface of a MaluOS agent (Phase 12 slice 8).

One protocol for an agent wherever it runs: JSON-RPC 2.0 over HTTP, shaped
like A2A (tasks/send, tasks/get, tasks/list, agent/card). A local agent
serves it on a Unix socket in its runtime directory
(MALUOS_AGENT_TASKS_SOCKET, /run/maluos/agents/NAME/tasks.sock) and answers
only its owner, root and itself (SO_PEERCRED, no token); an office serves
the same methods for its agents over HTTPS with the desk token. The Agents
app and `maluctl agent send` are the clients; Phase 13 slice 2 puts the
delegation envelope on it.

Server, in an agent:

    import maluos_agent_tasks as tasks
    def handle(task):                      # task = {"id", "text", "parts": [...], "ts", "progress"}
        task["progress"]("thinking…")      # partial text, shown while the task works (slice 9)
        return "the answer"                # or {"text": ..., "artifacts": [...]}
    tasks.serve(handle, card={"name": "Research", "description": "...", "capabilities": ["research"]})

serve() returns at once (a daemon thread); tasks run one at a time in order.
A task is {"id", "state": submitted|working|completed|failed, "ts", "input": {"text"},
"output": {"text", "artifacts"}, "error", "done_ts"}. While it works, output.text
is whatever the handler reported through progress() so far (slice 9: answers
stream); the final return value replaces it.

Client:

    c = tasks.Client.local("research")     # or tasks.Client(url, token) for an office agent
    c.card(); c.send("summarise ..."); c.get(id); c.list()
    c.stream("summarise ...", on_text)     # send without waiting, poll tasks/get, on_text(text) as it grows
"""
import http.client, json, os, pwd, socket, struct, sys, threading, time, urllib.parse, uuid
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer
from socketserver import UnixStreamServer

VERSION = "0.2"
SOCKET_DIR = "/run/maluos/agents"


def socket_path(name=None):
    if name:
        return f"{SOCKET_DIR}/{name}/tasks.sock"
    return os.environ.get("MALUOS_AGENT_TASKS_SOCKET") or (f"{SOCKET_DIR}/{os.environ['MALUOS_AGENT']}/tasks.sock" if os.environ.get("MALUOS_AGENT") else None)


def _owner_uid():
    o = os.environ.get("MALUOS_AGENT_OWNER") or ""
    if o.startswith("user:"):
        try:
            return pwd.getpwnam(o[5:]).pw_uid
        except KeyError:
            pass
    return None


class TaskError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, code, message):
        super().__init__(message); self.code, self.message = code, message

def enroll(a):
    need_root()
    if not a or a[0].startswith("-"):
        sys.exit("usage: maluctl office enroll URL --code CODE [--name N] [--owner LOGIN] [--no-gateway]")
    url = a.pop(0).rstrip("/")
    if not url.startswith(("http://", "https://")):
        sys.exit(f"the office URL must start with http:// or https:// ({url})")
    code = opt(a, "--code") or sys.exit("--code CODE: the one-time enrolment code the office shows the person")
    name = opt(a, "--name"); owner = opt(a, "--owner") or os.environ.get("SUDO_USER")
    no_gw = opt(a, "--no-gateway", flag=True); force = opt(a, "--force", flag=True)
    if not owner or owner == "root":
        sys.exit("--owner LOGIN: whose desk this is (or run sudo from that account)")
    try:
        pwd.getpwnam(owner)
    except KeyError:
        sys.exit(f"no such user {owner}")
    old = read_conf()
    if old and not force:
        sys.exit(f"this desk is already enrolled with {old.get('url')} as desk #{(old.get('desk') or {}).get('id')}; `sudo maluctl office leave` first, or --force")
    principal = f"user:{owner}"
    who = run_as(owner, ["secret", "whoami"], check=False)
    if f"principal:  {principal}" not in who:
        sys.exit(f"{owner} is not an enrolled principal on this host (sudo maluctl principal add {principal} --kind human)")
    body = {"surface": SURFACE, "code": code, "name": name, "principal": principal, **facts()}
    try:
        st, r = http("POST", url + "/api/v1/desks/enroll", body)
    except Exception as e:
        sys.exit(f"cannot reach the office at {url}: {str(e)[:160]}")
    if st not in (200, 201):
        sys.exit(f"the office refused enrolment ({st} {r.get('error') or ''}): {r.get('message') or r}")
    token, desk, eps = r.get("token"), r.get("desk") or {}, r.get("endpoints") or {}
    if not token or not desk.get("id"):
        sys.exit("the office answered without a desk token or a desk id")
    # 1. the token, into the owner's own compartment (as them: peer identity, their ledger rows)
    run_as(owner, ["secret", "delete", SECRET], check=False)
    run_as(owner, ["secret", "add", SECRET, "--kind", "token", "--provider", "office", "--env", "MALUOS_OFFICE_TOKEN", "--stdin"], input=token + "\n")
    conf = {"surface": r.get("surface", SURFACE), "url": url, "office": r.get("office") or {"name": None, "url": url}, "desk": desk,
            "owner": {**(r.get("owner") or {}), "login": owner, "principal": principal}, "endpoints": eps,
            "heartbeat_s": int(r.get("heartbeat_s") or 300), "secret": SECRET, "gateway": None, "enrolled_at": utc(), "maluos_desk": VERSION}
    # 2. the office's models as a rung of this desk's gateway, keyed by the token the gateway applies for the caller
    models = eps.get("models") if isinstance(eps.get("models"), dict) else None
    gw_note = "the office publishes no model endpoint to desks"
    if models and models.get("url") and not no_gw:
        mlist = [m for m in (models.get("models") or []) if m]
        try:
            # The rung names the owner's token explicitly (slice 9): a principal without a grant is refused by the
            # vault and asks the owner (a grant request with the call as its cause), instead of "no such secret".
            gateway(["backend", "add", "office", "--kind", "openai_compat", "--endpoint", models["url"].rstrip("/"), "--secret", f"{principal}/{SECRET}"]
                    + (["--models", ",".join(mlist)] if mlist else []))
            gateway(["tier", "add", "office", "--description", "the office's models, through the desk token"])
            if mlist:

            gw_note = f"maluctl gateway chat ... --model office  ({', '.join(mlist) or 'models as the office lists them'})"
        except Exception as e:
            gw_note

### MaluOS vault and gateway (2026-11-02)

The vault and gateway protocols are not undocumented after all: their sources are installed
(`/usr/lib/maluos/maluos_vault.py`, `/usr/lib/maluos/maluos_gateway/`). Both are HTTP + JSON over Unix sockets; the vault
identifies callers by `SO_PEERCRED` and the owner (`user:maludb`) is enrolled; the gateway has OpenAI and Anthropic faces
with tools and streaming. What Slides builds and what it asks of the MaluOS build is in
[maluos-integration.md](maluos-integration.md).

## Phase 4: slides-specific depth
---
## Asks of the MaluOS build (the gap)

1. **Vault read contract for desktop apps**: confirm an owner's process may read its own
   secret with `mode=read` and no reauth; fix the naming convention apps use to find a provider
   key (proposal: match `provider` = `anthropic` / `openai`, fall back to `env_var`;
   `maluctl secret add` sets both). Confirm `MALUOS_VAULT_SOCKET` as the override for tests.
2. **Gateway field coverage**: which request fields survive the translation to the canonical
   body on each face. Slides sends, on `/v1/messages`: `stream`, `system`, `tools` with
   `input_schema`, `max_tokens`, `thinking: {type: adaptive}`, `output_config.effort`, signed
   `thinking` blocks in the history, `anthropic-version` / `anthropic-beta` headers, and reads
   `usage.cache_read_input_tokens`; on `/v1/chat/completions`: `tools`, `stream`,
   `stream_options.include_usage`, `max_completion_tokens`, `reasoning_effort`. State which are
   passed through, mapped or dropped, so Slides knows when to go direct.
3. **Catalogue**: add the Claude 5 family (`claude-opus-5-5`, `claude-sonnet-5-5`,
   `claude-haiku-5-5`) and `gpt-5.1` as backends/aliases, or document how a desktop adds them
   (`maluctl gateway alias set …`).
4. **Provisioning**: a documented or first-boot step that stores the owner's provider keys
   (`maluctl secret add …`) and registers the cloud backends with `--secret`, and a default
   policy for the owner's principal (`maluctl gateway policy set --principal user:<login> --cloud
   yes`, budgets). Today none of this is done on a fresh desktop.
5. **Docs**: `docs/phase6-slice1-vault.md` and `docs/inference-node-api.md` are cited by the
   sources but not installed; ship them under `/usr/share/doc/maluos-vault/` and
   `/usr/share/doc/maluos-gateway/`, or give the repository path.
6. **Dev mode**: a way to run both services in CI headless (`--kind mock` backend exists for the
   gateway); env overrides for both sockets; a non-root way to enrol a test principal.

## 🤖 Claude

`maludb-os-docker` is not what Slides needs, and it cannot be installed on this desk, so I did not install it. Findings are recorded in the integration and status docs, committed as `ee0d7782` and pushed.

**What the repository is.** It installs the Business OS kernel plus Help Desk and Spaces as one container on a MaluDB hosting VM. That is the office side. Its install script refuses any host that is not a hosting VM. It checks for Ubuntu 24.04, PostgreSQL 17, the MaluDB API on port 8000, a tenant database config under `/var/www`, and a public FQDN. This desk is MaluOS 26.04 with PostgreSQL 18 and none of the rest. The script would also need your sudo password, stop Apache and edit the PostgreSQL access rules. Its Claude Code plugin covers Business OS application development, not this app.

**What Slides actually needs for 4.5.** The desk package already ships everything on the client side. A desk enrols with an office by URL and one-time code. The office publishes an agents directory. Each agent takes tasks over a small JSON-RPC protocol and returns an answer with artifacts, which is where a picture would arrive. The Phase 13 delegation envelope is mentioned in the installed code but not shipped yet, so the desk token alone authorises a task today.

**The current state of this desk.**

- Not enrolled with any office.
- No office agent with an image capability exists yet, including in the shipped mock, whose two agents answer text only.
- The vault and gateway run and answer. The "unhealthy" vault line in `maluctl status` is a stale result from the October provisioning run.

**What I set up.** The mock office that ships with the desk package now runs as the user service `maluos-mock-office` on port 18080 with enrolment code `slides-dev`. I verified its contract with a throwaway desk and retired it. Enrolling this desk requires root once, so that one is yours to run:

```
! sudo maluctl office enroll http://127.0.0.1:18080 --code slides-dev --name "Ed's desk"
```

**What this means for 4.5.** I can build it against the task protocol as it exists, choosing an agent by capability rather than a fixed id, and test it with a mock image agent inside the assist crate. Live verification against a real image agent waits on the office. I added that as ask 7 in `docs/maluos-slides/maluos-integration.md` for the MaluOS build process.

Next step is 4.5 on that basis, or 4.6 if you prefer the step with no platform dependency.

"""Client for the MaluOS vault over its Unix socket. Identity is the calling
process's uid (peer credentials); nothing to configure. Used by maluctl, the
first-boot components and, from slice 2, the inference gateway."""
import http.client, json, os, socket, urllib.parse

SOCKET = os.environ.get("MALUOS_VAULT_SOCKET", "/run/maluos/vault.sock")


class VaultError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, status, code, message):
        super().__init__(f"{code}: {message}"); self.status, self.code, self.message = status, code, message


class _UnixConn(http.client.HTTPConnection):
    def __init__(self, path, timeout=30):
        super().__init__("maluos-vault", timeout=timeout); self.path = path

    def connect(self):
        s = socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX, socket.SOCK_STREAM); s.settimeout(self.timeout); s.connect(self.path); self.sock = s


class Vault:
    def __init__(self, socket_path=None, on_behalf_of=None, timeout=30):
        self.socket_path, self.on_behalf_of, self.timeout = socket_path or SOCKET, on_behalf_of, timeout

    def request(self, method, path, body=None, query=None):
        if query:
            path += "?" + urllib.parse.urlencode({k: v for k, v in query.items() if v not in (None, "", False)})
        headers = {"Content-Type": "application/json"}
        if self.on_behalf_of:
            headers["X-MaluOS-Principal"] = self.on_behalf_of
        data = json.dumps(body).encode() if body is not None else None
        c = _UnixConn(self.socket_path, self.timeout)
        try:
            c.request(method, path, body=data, headers=headers)
            r = c.getresponse(); raw = r.read()
        except (FileNotFoundError, ConnectionRefusedError) as e:
            raise VaultError(0, "unavailable", f"vault socket {self.socket_path}: {e.strerror or e}")
        finally:
            c.close()
        try:
            obj = json.loads(raw) if raw else {}
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            raise VaultError(r.status, "bad_response", raw[:200].decode(errors="replace"))
        if r.status >= 400:
            raise VaultError(r.status, obj.get("error", "error"), obj.get("message", ""))
        return obj

    def available(self):
        return os.path.exists(self.socket_path)

    # convenience
    def health(self):             return self.request("GET", "/v1/health")
    def whoami(self):             return self.request("GET", "/v1/whoami")
    def compartments(self):       return self.request("GET", "/v1/compartments")["compartments"]
    def create_compartment(self, name, owner=None, scope=None, lock_mode=None):
        return self.request("POST", "/v1/compartments", {"name": name, "owner": owner, "scope": scope, "lock_mode": lock_mode})
    def lock(self, name, locked=True):
        return self.request("POST", f"/v1/compartments/{q(name)}/{'lock' if locked else 'unlock'}")
    def secrets(self, compartment=None, all=False):

[package]
name = "maluos-slides-assist"
version.workspace = true
edition.workspace = true
license.workspace = true
description = "MaluOS Slides assistant: the tool table shared with the MCP server, the command catalog and its schemas, tool execution through engine commands"

[lints]
workspace = true

[features]
default = ["native"]
# The real clients (ureq); off on wasm32, where the policy, catalog and loop still compile.

[dependencies]
maluos-slides-engine = { workspace = true }
maluos-slides-mcp = { workspace = true }
maluos-llm = { workspace = true, default-features = false }
serde = { workspace = true }
serde_json = { workspace = true }
log = { workspace = true }
---
//! The MaluOS Slides assistant (plan `docs/maluos-slides/plan.md`, Phase 3).
//!
//! This crate is fork code: it sits beside upstream's crates and never edits them. It gives the
//! assistant the same view of the application the MCP server has, so one table drives both
//! (owner decision D9):
//!
//! - [`ToolTable`]: the MCP tool definitions (`maluos_slides_mcp::tool_definitions`) as
//!   [`maluos_llm::ToolDef`]s a model can call, minus the tools a backend without a window cannot
//!   serve.
//! - [`Catalog`]: every engine command with its label, params doc and a JSON Schema generated from
//!   that doc (`maluos_slides_engine::cmd::parse_params`), so `run_command` calls are checked
//!   before they run and the model can be shown a compact listing.
//! - [`Context`]: the open deck as an outline for the prompt (sections, titles, placeholder
//!   text, notes, the selection, the theme), cut to a budget, cached on the revision.
//! - [`Assistant::ask`]: the loop (step 3.4): prompt, model, tool calls, results, answer, one
//!   undo entry per turn, limits on rounds, tool calls and tokens, retries on retryable errors.
//! - [`Policy`] (step 3.5): the modes answer-only, confirm and autopilot; destructive commands
//!   always confirmed; plans the user approves through [`Confirm`].
//! - [`outline`] (step 4.1): a deck from Markdown or a slide list, the `build_deck` tool, and
//!   [`mcp_ext::Server`], the MCP server with the fork's tools added.
//! - [`timing`] (step 4.4): how long a deck takes, per slide and in total, and the cue line
//!   presenter view shows; the `deck_timing` tool.
//! - [`run_tool`]: one tool call executed through an MCP [`Backend`] (the headless session or a
//!   running app), the result shaped as the tool-result block the next request carries.
//!
//! Everything the assistant does to a deck goes through `Session::execute` behind the backend; it
//! never touches the model directly. The loop that ties this to an `LlmClient` is step 3.4.
#![deny(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::panic, clippy::unimplemented, clippy::todo, clippy::unreachable)]
#![forbid(unsafe_code)]

pub mod agent;
pub mod catalog;

    /// What one call does and the commands behind it.
    pub fn classify(&self, table: &ToolTable, catalog: &Catalog, tool_use_id: &str, name: &str, input: &Value) -> PlannedCall {
        let mut commands = Vec::new();
        let mut class = if table.is_read_only(name) { Class::ReadOnly } else { Class::Change };
        let mut note = |id: &str, params: Value, class: &mut Class| {
            let (label, query) = catalog.get(id).map(|e| (e.label.to_string(), e.is_query())).unwrap_or_else(|| (String::new(), false));
            let c = if self.is_destructive_command(id) {
                Class::Destructive
            } else if query {
                Class::ReadOnly
            } else {
                Class::Change
            };
            *class = (*class).max(c);
            commands.push((id.to_string(), label, params));
        };
        match name {
            "run_command" => {
                class = Class::ReadOnly;
                let id = input.get("command").and_then(Value::as_str).unwrap_or("");
                note(id, input.get("params").cloned().unwrap_or(Value::Null), &mut class);
            }
            "batch" => {
                class = Class::ReadOnly;
                for c in input.get("commands").and_then(Value::as_array).into_iter().flatten() {
                    let id = c.get("command").and_then(Value::as_str).unwrap_or("");
                    note(id, c.get("params").cloned().unwrap_or(Value::Null), &mut class);
                }
            }
            _ => {
                if self.destructive_tools.iter().any(|t| t == name)
                    || (name == crate::tools::BUILD_DECK && input.get("replace").and_then(Value::as_bool).unwrap_or(false))
                {
                    class = Class::Destructive;
                }
                if let Some(id) = tool_command(name) {
                    let label = catalog.get(id).map(|e| e.label.to_string()).unwrap_or_default();
                    commands.push((id.to_string(), label, input.clone()));
                }
            }
        }
        PlannedCall { tool_use_id: tool_use_id.into(), name: name.into(), input: input.clone(), class, commands }
    }

    pub fn decide(&self, class: Class) -> Decision {
        match (self.mode, class) {
            (_, Class::ReadOnly) => Decision::Allow,
            (Mode::AnswerOnly, _) => {
                Decision::Refuse("answer-only mode: the presentation cannot be changed now; tell the user what you would do".into())
            }
            (Mode::Confirm, _) => Decision::Confirm,
            (Mode::Autopilot, Class::Change) => Decision::Allow,
            (Mode::Autopilot, Class::Destructive) => Decision::Confirm,
        }
    }
}

//! Tests run the tool table and the catalog against the headless engine; no model, no network.
#![allow(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::panic)]

use std::path::PathBuf;

use maluos_llm::ContentBlock;
use maluos_slides_engine::command_specs;
use maluos_slides_mcp::{Backend, Headless};
use serde_json::{Value, json};

use crate::{Catalog, MAX_RESULT_BYTES, ToolTable, params_schema, run_tool};

/// Compares `text` with `snapshots/<name>`; `MALUOS_SLIDES_UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1` rewrites it.
fn assert_snapshot(name: &str, text: &str) {
    let path = PathBuf::from(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("snapshots").join(name);
    if std::env::var_os("MALUOS_SLIDES_UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS").is_some() {
        std::fs::write(&path, text).unwrap();
        return;
    }
    let want = std::fs::read_to_string(&path).unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("{}: {e} (MALUOS_SLIDES_UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1 writes it)", path.display()));
    if want != text {
        let diff: Vec<String> = want
            .lines()
            .zip(text.lines())
            .enumerate()
            .filter(|(_, (a, b))| a != b)
            .take(5)
            .map(|(i, (a, b))| format!("line {}:\n  - {a}\n  + {b}", i + 1))
            .collect();
        panic!(
            "{} differs ({} vs {} lines):\n{}\nMALUOS_SLIDES_UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1 rewrites it",
            path.display(),
            want.lines().count(),
            text.lines().count(),
            diff.join("\n")
        );
    }
}

fn pretty(v: &Value) -> String {
    let mut s = serde_json::to_string_pretty(v).unwrap();
    s.push('\n');
    s
}

fn session() -> Headless {
    Headless::with_document()
}

fn slide_count(h: &Headless) -> usize {
    h.session.active().unwrap().doc.slides.len()
}

// ---------- the tool table ----------

#[test]

fn usage(input: u64, output: u64) -> Usage {

}

fn tool_use(id: &str, name: &str, input: Value) -> ContentBlock {
    ContentBlock::ToolUse { id: id.into(), name: name.into(), input }
}

fn calls(blocks: Vec<ContentBlock>) -> Completion {
    Completion { model: "mock".into(), content: blocks, stop_reason: StopReason::ToolUse, usage: usage(100, 20) }
}

fn answer(text: &str) -> Completion {
    Completion {
        model: "mock".into(),
        content: vec![ContentBlock::Text { text: text.into() }],
        stop_reason: StopReason::EndTurn,
        usage: usage(100, 10),
    }
}

//! The native transport: `ureq` with rustls, no async runtime, streaming reads.

use std::time::Duration;

use crate::LlmError;
use crate::transport::{HttpRequest, HttpResponse, Transport};

/// Posts with `ureq`. One agent per client; connections are reused.
pub struct UreqTransport {
    agent: ureq::Agent,
}

impl Default for UreqTransport {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new(Duration::from_secs(30), Duration::from_secs(180))
    }
}

impl UreqTransport {
    /// `connect` bounds the TCP and TLS handshake; `per_read` bounds the wait for the next byte
    /// of a streaming reply (a model that stops producing tokens for that long is given up on).
    /// There is no whole-request timeout: long answers stream for minutes.
    pub fn new(connect: Duration, per_read: Duration) -> Self {
        let config = ureq::Agent::config_builder()
            .http_status_as_error(false)
            .timeout_connect(Some(connect))
            .timeout_per_read(Some(per_read))
            .timeout_send_request(Some(connect))
            .timeout_recv_response(Some(per_read))
            .user_agent("maluos-llm")
            .build();
        UreqTransport { agent: config.new_agent() }
    }
}

impl Transport for UreqTransport {
    fn post(&self, request: &HttpRequest) -> Result<HttpResponse, LlmError> {
        let mut builder = self.agent.post(&request.url);
        for (name, value) in &request.headers {
            builder = builder.header(name.as_str(), value.as_str());
        }
        let response = builder.send(request.body.as_str()).map_err(|e| match e {
            ureq::Error::Timeout(_) => LlmError::Transport(format!("timed out: {e}")),
            other => LlmError::Transport(other.to_string()),
        })?;
        let status = response.status().as_u16();
        let headers =
            response.headers().iter().map(|(k, v)| (k.as_str().to_ascii_lowercase(), String::from_utf8_lossy(v.as_bytes()).into_owned())).collect();
        let body = response.into_body().into_reader();
        Ok(HttpResponse { status, headers, body: Box::new(body) })
    }
}

/// The standing instructions. The catalog and the deck outline follow them in the system text.
pub const INSTRUCTIONS: &str = "You are Malu, the assistant inside MaluOS Slides, a presentation editor. You help the user build and change the open presentation by calling tools; every change goes through the editor's own commands and the user can undo a whole turn at once.

How to work:
- The deck outline below is the state right now: it is rebuilt after every tool call, so changes you made earlier in this turn already show in it (do not take them for pre-existing content). Slides are numbered from 1 in prose but tools take 0-based indexes and shape ids; both are in the outline.
- When the user says \"this\", \"here\" or \"the title\", the selection is the target; without a selection, the current slide is.
- To change text, use set_text with the shape id (it keeps the formatting). To add content, use add_slide, add_shape, add_text_box, insert_table or insert_chart. For a whole deck or several slides at once, write the outline and call build_deck once (Markdown: # title, ## section, ### slide, - bullets, Notes: lines, | tables |); it makes the title slide, sections, slides, notes and tables in one call. When the user gives a document, build the deck from its content: one idea per slide, five bullets at most, a title slide, sections for its parts, a closing slide. For anything else, run_command with a command id from the catalog; its params are documented there. Use batch for several commands.
- Check the result of a tool before building on it: inspect_slide shows ids and boxes, render_slide shows the picture (it is attached to the result when you can see images; look at it after a visual change).

Slide help, the usual requests:
- Tighten a title: set_text on the title placeholder (ctrTitle or title in the outline), at most six words, no trailing period.
- Rewrite bullets: set_text on the body placeholder with the whole body: at most five bullets, parallel phrasing, each under twelve words, keep the levels with leading tabs, keep facts and numbers as they are.
- Speaker notes: run_command slide.notes {text, index?} with three to six spoken sentences that add what the slide does not say; never repeat the bullets.
- A chart from a table: inspect_slide for every cell; the first column is the categories, each numeric column a series; insert_chart with a matching type (column for comparisons over categories, line for a series over time, pie only for parts of one whole with at most six slices); keep the table unless asked to replace it.
- Timing: deck_timing gives seconds per slide and the total; to fit a time limit, cut the longest slides' notes and bullets first, never the title or closing slide.
- Q&A prep (prepare me for questions): read the whole deck (inspect_document, then inspect_slide where the outline is cut), write six to ten questions an audience would ask with a two-sentence answer each drawn only from the deck (say 'not in the deck' when it is not), and put them on one new slide at the end titled Q&A prep, questions as bullets and the answers in its notes, then hide it with run_command slide.hide {hidden: true} so it never shows.
- Fix a layout: the outline gives each shape's box [x, y, w, h] on a 960×540 slide; align edges and spacing with shape.move / shape.resize through run_command (list_commands with the filter align shows arrange.align and arrange.distribute), use format.autofit {mode: shrink} for text that overflows, and render_slide to confirm.
- Make the smallest change that does what was asked; keep the deck's theme, layouts and style unless asked otherwise.
- Answer briefly: what changed, on which slides. Do not describe tool mechanics. If something cannot be done, say so.";

pub fn tool_command(tool: &str) -> Option<&'static str> {
    Some(match tool {
        "new_presentation" => "file.new",
        "open_presentation" => "file.open",
        "save_presentation" => "file.save",
        "export" => "file.export",
        "inspect_slide" => "slide.inspect",
        "add_slide" => "slide.new",
        "go_to_slide" => "slide.go",
        "add_shape" => "shape.insert",
        "add_text_box" => "insert.textBox",
        "set_text" => "text.set",
        "insert_picture" => "insert.picture",
        "insert_table" => "insert.table",
        "insert_chart" => "insert.chart",
        "select" => "edit.select",
        "build_deck" => "slide.new",
        "deck_timing" => "document.inspect",
        _ => return None,
    })

fn short(v: &Value) -> String {
    let s = match v {
        Value::String(s) => format!("{s:?}"),
        other => other.to_string(),
    };
    if s.chars().count() > 60 { s.chars().take(59).chain(std::iter::once('…')).collect() } else { s }

/// server and the assistant never disagree on a name, a schema or a description.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct ToolTable {
    tools: Vec<ToolDef>,
    read_only: BTreeSet<String>,
    app_only: BTreeSet<String>,
}

impl ToolTable {
    /// Every tool, including the ones that need a window.
    pub fn all() -> Self {
        Self::build(true)
    }

    /// The tools a backend can serve: without a UI the app-only tools (`screenshot`,
    /// `call_app`) are left out, so the model is never offered a call that cannot succeed.
    pub fn for_backend(has_ui: bool) -> Self {
        Self::build(has_ui)
    }

    fn build(with_app_only: bool) -> Self {
        let mut tools = Vec::new();
        let mut read_only = BTreeSet::new();
        let mut app_only = BTreeSet::new();
        for def in maluos_slides_mcp::tool_definitions().into_iter().chain(extra_definitions()) {
            let Some(tool) = to_llm(&def) else { continue };
            let is_app_only = tool.description.contains(APP_ONLY_MARKER);
            if is_app_only {
                app_only.insert(tool.name.clone());
                if !with_app_only {
                    continue;
                }
            }
            if def.pointer("/annotations/readOnlyHint").and_then(Value::as_bool).unwrap_or(false) {
                read_only.insert(tool.name.clone());
            }
            tools.push(tool);
        }
        ToolTable { tools, read_only, app_only }
    }

    /// The definitions, in the MCP server's order, ready for `Request::with_tools`.
    pub fn defs(&self) -> &[ToolDef] {
        &self.tools
    }

    pub fn get(&self, name: &str) -> Option<&ToolDef> {
        self.tools.iter().find(|t| t.name == name)
    }

    pub fn names(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &str> {
        self.tools.iter().map(|t| t.name.as_str())
    }

    /// The MCP server marks it `readOnlyHint`: it changes nothing.
    pub fn is_read_only(&self, name: &str) -> bool {
        self.read_only.contains(name)
    }

    /// It needs the desktop app (a backend with a UI).
    pub fn is_app_only(&self, name: &str) -> bool {
        self.app_only.contains(name)
    }

    /// The raw MCP definitions (name, title, description, `inputSchema`, annotations), upstream's
    /// and the fork's, for a network API that wants to publish the same table.
    pub fn mcp_definitions() -> Vec<Value> {
        let mut v = maluos_slides_mcp::tool_definitions();
        v.extend(extra_definitions());
        v
    }

    /// The fork's own definitions.
    pub fn extra_definitions() -> Vec<Value> {
        extra_definitions()
    }

    pub fn is_extra(name: &str) -> bool {
        is_extra(name)
    }
}

/// One MCP definition as a [`ToolDef`]; `None` when it lacks a name.
fn to_llm(def: &Value) -> Option<ToolDef> {
    let name = def.get("name").and_then(Value::as_str)?.to_string();
    let description = def.get("description").and_then(Value::as_str).unw

head_end = raw.windows(4).position(|w| w == b\"\\r\\n\\r\\n\").ok_or_else(|| std::io::Error::other(\"no HTTP header in the answer\"))?;\n    let head = String::from_utf8_lossy(&raw[..head_end]).into_owned();\n    let status = head.lines().next().and_then(|l| l.split_whitespace().nth(1)).and_then(|s| s.parse().ok()).unwrap_or(0);\n    let mut body = raw[head_end + 4..].to_vec();\n    if let Some(len) = head.lines().find_map(|l| {\n        let (k, v) = l.split_once(':')?;\n        k.eq_ignore_ascii_case(\"content-length\").then(|| v.trim().parse::<usize>().ok())?\n    }) {\n        body.truncate(len);\n    }\n    Ok((status, body))\n}\n\n// ---------- the office over HTTP ----------\n\nfn agent_for(timeout: Duration) -> ureq::Agent {\n    ureq::Agent::config_builder()\n        .http_status_as_error(false)\n        .timeout_connect(Some(Duration::from_secs(20)))\n        .timeout_global(Some(timeout + Duration::from_secs(30)))\n        .user_agent(\"maluos-slides\")\n        .build()\n        .new_agent()\n}\n\nfn http_json(method: &str, url: &str, token: &str, body: Option<&Value>, timeout: Duration) -> Result<Value, OfficeError> {\n    let agent = agent_for(timeout);\n    let bearer = format!(\"Bearer {token}\");\n    let result = match (method, body) {\n        (\"POST\", Some(b)) => agent\n            .post(url)\n            .header(\"Authorization\", &bearer)\n            .header(\"Accept\", \"application/json\")\n            .header(\"Content-Type\", \"application/json\")\n            .send(b.to_string().as_str()),\n        _ => agent.get(url).header(\"Authorization\", &bearer).header(\"Accept\", \"application/json\").call(),\n    };\n    let mut response = result.map_err(|e| OfficeError::Office(format!(\"{url}: {e}\")))?;\n    let status = response.status().as_u16();\n    let text = response.body_mut().read_to_string().map_err(|e| OfficeError::Office(format!(\"{url}: {e}\")))?;\n    let v: Value = serde_json::from_str(&text).map_err(|_| OfficeError::Office(format!(\"{url}: {status} {}\", text.chars().take(160).collect::<String>())))?;\n    if status >= 400 {\n        let msg = v.get(\"message\").or_else(|| v.get(\"error\")).map(|m| m.as_str().map(str::to_string).unwrap_or_else(|| m.to_string())).unwrap_or_default();\n        return Err(OfficeError::Office(format!(\"{url}: {status} {msg}\")));\n    }\n    Ok(v)\n}\n\nfn http_bytes(url: &str, token: &str, timeout: Duration) -> .call()\n        .map_err(|e| OfficeError::Office(format!(\"{url}: {e}\")))?;\n    let status = response.status().as_u16();\n    if status >= 400 {\n        return The assistant pane (step 3.6, 2026-11-02) lives in `crates/ui-egui/src/malu_assistant.rs`; the
app build is `target/debug/maluos-slides`. Launch on the desktop with
`target/debug/maluos-slides --sample --control 7990`, then script it through the control
channel: `maluos-slides-cli app --port 7990 --method engine.execute
'{"command":"assist.ask","params":{"text":"…","send":true}}'`, answer plans with
`assist.plan {"verdict":"approve"}`, screenshot with `ui.screenshot {"path":…}`. Provider
defaults to the first one with a key, else Ollama (`glm-5.3-flash:cloud` works here).
Kill only my own instance: `pgrep -f "^target/debug/maluos-slides "` (a `pkill -f` pattern that
also matches the shell kills the shell). The owner's installed `/usr/bin/maluos-slides` is a
separate old build.

**Why:** the owner wants to see the app state at each stopping point, not a terminal transcript.
**How to apply:** at the end of a UI step, launch the app, drive a live turn, screenshot into
`docs/maluos-slides/screenshots/`, link them from status.md. See [[product-vision-cursor-for-slides]].

### Phase 5: parity through upstream
---
## The presenter assistant (step 4.4)

`timing.rs` estimates how long a deck takes: for each slide the words on it (text, tables,
groups) and in its notes, seconds = 8 + notes ÷ 130 wpm + slide text ÷ 60 wpm, at least 15;
the total counts shown slides only. Presenter view shows "≈ 1:20 · deck 14:30" beside the slide
counter and a cue line (the notes' first sentences, 30 words) above the full notes. The
read-only tool `deck_timing` gives the model the same numbers, through `document.inspect` and
`slide.inspect` so it also works on a running app. The instructions add two recipes: timing
(trim the longest slides' notes and bullets first) and Q&A prep (six to ten questions with
answers drawn only from the deck, on one hidden slide at the end, answers in its notes); the
pane offers Q&A prep as a quick action.

## Snapshots

`snapshots/tools.json` is the tool table (every tool, app-only included),
`snapshots/commands.json` the catalog with each command's generated schema, and
`snapshots/context-sample.md` the outline of the sample deck (`engine::sample`) on slide 2. The tests compare
against them; `MALUOS_SLIDES_UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1 cargo nextest run -p maluos-slides-assist`
rewrites them after a deliberate change (an upstream merge that adds or re-documents a command
shows up here as a diff to read, not a failure to silence).

## Tests

`cargo nextest run -p maluos-slides-assist`: 31 tests. The table mirrors the server definition
for definition; the headless table drops the app-only tools; every one of the engine's params
docs parses into a schema (a guard against upstream drift in the grammar); schema rules on hand-
written docs; validation of unknown commands, keys and non-object params; the prompt listing's
filter and cut; and, on the headless engine, tool calls that add and inspect slides, a
`run_command` that pushes one undo step, refusals that leave the revision untouched, image and
long-result shaping. For the context: the sample-deck snapshot, no document, the selection and an edited text range, a 121-slide deck cut at a small budget with the current slide whole and every marker present, and the cache rebuilding only

{
  "file_path": "/home/maludb/maluos-slides/docs/maluos-slides/harness-design.md",
  "content": "# The MaluOS office harness: design decisions shared by Slides, Malu123 and MaluDocs\n\nThe owner's direction (2026-11-03): the same process that turns MaluOS Slides into an AI harness\nwill be run for **Malu123** (a spreadsheet, like Excel) and **MaluDocs** (a document editor,\nlike Word). This document records every design decision taken in Slides so the three\napplications end up consistent in design and function. Each decision says what was decided, why,\nhow it shows in Slides, and what the other two should mirror. Slides-specific detail lives in\n[assistant.md](assistant.md), [llm.md](llm.md), [api.md](api.md), [cli.md](cli.md) and\n[maluos-integration.md](maluos-integration.md); this file is the cross-application contract.\n\nNumbering: `H<n>` (harness). Owner decisions from the plan keep their `D<n>` ids.\n\n## 1. Shape of the work\n\n| Id | Decision | Why | Mirror in Malu123 / MaluDocs |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| H1 | **Fork, keep upstream mergeable.** Fork code lives in new crates (`maluos-<app>-assist`, `maluos-<app>-api`) and the shared `maluos-llm`; upstream crates are touched only for bug fixes worth sending upstream; UI and app hooks are fenced (`// MaluOS:` comments, one `pub mod` per feature). | Upstream keeps moving; a merge must stay a mechanical rename plus a few fenced hooks. | Same crate names with the app's prefix; same fence style; the rename script pattern (`scripts/rename-upstream.sh`, a vendor branch). |\n| H2 | **Plan and status files.** `docs/<app>/plan.md` holds phases and steps with \"done when\"; `docs/<app>/status.md` records what landed, with verification and live runs; commit ids are plan steps (`P4.5: …`). | The owner follows progress by stopping points, not by diffs. | Identical layout and wording; one row per step with the evidence. |\n| H3 | **Linux and MaluOS only** (owner D1). No other platform packaging or docs; platform `cfg` branches inside upstream crates stay as upstream has them. | One target, one image. | Same. |\n| H4 | **Gates before a push**: fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, nextest, doctests, asset attribution, layering, wasm check of the wasm-safe crates. Build under a memory scope so the desktop never starves. | A green tree at every stopping point. | Same xtask set; the layering table lists the assist crate at the UI layer and the API crate above it. |\n\n## 2. The engine is the only door\n\n| Id | Decision | Why | Mirror |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| H5 | **The assistant acts only through engine commands** (`Session::execute`), never through the model types. Every change is a command with params documented in a fixed grammar, parsed into a JSON Schema for the model. | Commands are the audited, undoable, scriptable surface; the model gets exactly what the user has. | Malu123: cell, range, sheet and formula commands; MaluDocs: paragraph, run, style, section commands. The params-doc grammar and the schema generator are shared code. |\n| H6 | **One undoable history group per turn.** Everything a turn did folds into one entry named after the request (`Assistant: add a closing slide…`); the pane shows Undo per turn. | The user judges a turn as a whole. | Same fold over the app's history type. |\n| H7 | **One tool table for the assistant, the HTTP API and MCP** (owner D9). The MCP server's definitions are the model's tools; the fork's extra tools are appended last and dispatched before upstream's `call_tool`; the API publishes the same table; an MCP wrapper adds the extras without editing upstream's server. | Three callers, one behaviour, one set of tests. | Same `ToolTable` / `extra_definitions` / `is_extra` / `mcp_ext::Server` pattern. |\n| H8 | **Tool conventions.** `snake_case` verb names; `readOnlyHint` decides the read-only class; a description marker (`Desktop app only`) hides tools a headless backend cannot serve; unknown arguments are refused by name with the allowed list; results are JSON text, errors are `is_error` text the model can act on; results are cut at 64 KiB with a marker. | The model learns one dialect across the apps. | Same markers, same error phrasing, same cut. |\n| H9 | **Validation before action.** `run_command` and `batch` calls are checked against the catalog (unknown command → did-you-mean by edit distance ≤ 2; undocumented keys refused) before anything runs. | A typo must not become a stray change. | Same catalog type. |\n\n## 3. Models and keys\n\n| Id | Decision | Why | Mirror |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| H10 | **`maluos-llm` is the one client**: a `Transport` trait with no async runtime, Anthropic Messages and OpenAI-compatible backends (OpenAI, Ollama, the gateway), streaming, tool use, images in tool results and user messages, a mock client and transport for tests, a `live` example for a real check. | One crate, shared by every app, fixed once. | Depend on it; add nothing app-specific to it. |\n| H11 | **Provider choice**: the first provider with a key in the environment, else Ollama at `127.0.0.1:11434`; the user may switch in the pane; the choice (provider, model, mode) is saved in `~/.config/maluos-<app>/assistant.json`, **never a key**. | Works out of the box on a MaluOS desktop with Ollama; cloud when the owner adds a key. | Same `providers::default_choice`, same config shape and path pattern. |\n| H12 | **Keys live in the MaluOS vault or an env var**, never in settings files, decks, documents or the repo. The vault is HTTP over its Unix socket with peer-credential identity; reads are `mode=read` with a `purpose`. | Platform rule. | Same `vault_value` code; the same purpose string pattern `\"<App>: <what for>\"`. |\n| H13 | **Limits per turn**: rounds 12, tool calls 40, output tokens 8000, catalog 32 KiB, retries 3 on rate-limit/overload (none on auth), messages trimmed at user turns to 60, images 6 per turn and dropped the turn after. | Bounded cost and a conversation that stays valid. | Same `Limits` defaults unless an app proves it needs others. |\n\n## 4. Context the model sees\n\n| Id | Decision | Why | Mirror |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| H14 | **System text = instructions + catalog + document outline.** The outline is rebuilt after every tool call (so the turn's own edits show), cut to a byte budget with explicit markers (`… [cut]`), the current unit kept whole, cached on (document id, revision, selection). | The model reasons on the real state; cost is bounded. | Slides: sections, slides, placeholders, notes, selection, theme. Malu123: sheets, used ranges, headers, the selected range's values and formulas, named ranges. MaluDocs: headings tree, the current section's paragraphs, styles, the selection. Same cut and cache mechanics. |\n| H15 | **Pictures to the model once per request**: a rendered slide rides with its `render_slide` result (both backends), and old pictures are stripped when a new turn starts. | Visual checks after visual changes without paying for them forever. | Malu123: a rendered range or chart; MaluDocs: a rendered page. Same stripping rule. |\n| H16 | **Indexes and ids**: prose numbers from 1, tools take 0-based indexes and shape ids; the outline shows both. | Models mix them up otherwise. | Same sentence in every app's instructions. |\n\n## 5. Safety rails\n\n| Id | Decision | Why | Mirror |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| H17 | **Three modes**: AnswerOnly (reads only, refuses changes with a sentence the model relays), Confirm (every change shown as a plan the user approves, declines with a reason the model hears, or stops), Autopilot (changes applied; destructive calls still confirmed). | The owner picks the trust level per session. | Same `Mode`, `Class`, `Decision`, `Plan`, `Confirm` trait. |\n| H18 | **Destructive is a list, not a guess**: named commands (delete, remove-all, file new/open/close/revert…) and tools (new/open, `build_deck` with `replace`). | Explicit, testable; an upstream merge that adds a command shows up in a snapshot diff. | Each app keeps its own list in `policy.rs`; the test asserts every name is a real command. |\n| H19 | **Nothing from the public web by default.** The assistant never fetches URLs; pictures come from the office's image agent only; an artifact given by URL is read only under the office's own URL. | Platform trust boundary; the owner's data stays in the estate. | Same rule and the same tool text (\"look nowhere else, never the web\"). |\n\n## 6. The pane and the app\n\n| Id | Decision | Why | Mirror |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| H20 | **The assistant is a side pane named \"Malu\"**, opened from a spark button in the title bar and `Cmd+Shift+A`, with provider, model and mode pickers, a status line (endpoint, key needed or not), a transcript with tool calls folded, a plan card (Approve / Decline / Stop), Undo per turn, and a request box (Enter sends). | \"Cursor for presentations\": the assistant beside the work, never a modal. | Same name, button, shortcut, layout and strings; the pane module is `malu_assistant.rs` in each app's UI crate. |\n| H21 | **Quick actions** for the usual requests on the current unit (\"This slide: Tighten title, Rewrite bullets, Write notes, Chart from table, Fix layout, Add a picture, Q&A prep\"): each fills the box with a fixed sentence and sends. | One click for the common cases; the sentences double as the recipes' test prompts. | Malu123: \"This sheet/range: Explain formula, Fill down, Clean data, Chart this, Add totals, Add a picture\". MaluDocs: \"This section: Tighten, Summarise, Fix headings, Write abstract, Table from text, Add a picture\". |\n| H22 | **Scriptable UI commands** `assist.ask {text?, send?, toggle?}` and `assist.plan {verdict, reason?}` through the app's control channel, so a test or the CLI drives the pane exactly as a user does. | Every user-visible action is a command with tests. | Same two commands. |\n| H23 | **Instructions are recipes**, one line each, naming the tool and the shape of the result (counts, limits, what never to touch). The persona is Malu; the answer is brief: what changed, where. | Short, testable, cheap. | Same opening paragraph and \"How to work\" block; recipes per app. |\n\n## 7. Surfaces: CLI, HTTP API, MCP\n\n| Id | Decision | Why | Mirror |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| H24 | **CLI verbs** `ask` (a turn against a file or the sample, `--mode`, `--yes`, `--provider`, `--model`, `--json`, `--from DOC`), `api` (serve), `mcp` (stdio server with the extras), plus app-specific builders (`outline` in Slides). | Headless use and CI. | Same verbs and flags; the builder verb is the app's natural input (`outline` → `csv`/`table` for Malu123, `markdown` for MaluDocs). |\n| H25 | **HTTP API** `/v1`: `health`, `tools` (the table), `tools/{name}` (one call), `commands[/{id}]`, `document`, the unit routes (`slides/{i}[/render.png]`), `ask`; loopback only unless a bearer token is set; hand-written HTTP/1.1, no async. | One API shape for every app's integrations and for the office's agents. | Same routes with the unit renamed (`sheets/{name}/ranges/{a1}`, `sections/{i}`), same token rule. |\n| H26 | **MCP** is upstream's server wrapped: the fork's tools appended to `tools/list` and answered on `tools/call`. | Keeps the upstream server untouched. | Same wrapper. |\n\n## 8. The platform: vault, gateway, office\n\n| Id | Decision | Why | Mirror |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| H27 | **Integration follows the installed sources**, never guesses: `/usr/lib/maluos/*.py` and `maluctl` define the vault, gateway, desk and task protocols. ## 🤖 Claude

Phase 4.5 is done, committed as `5b69c96a` and pushed. The app is still open on your desktop showing the result.

**What landed.**

- **An office client** in the assist crate. It reads the desk's enrolment file, takes the desk token from the environment variable the platform defines or from the vault over its Unix socket, lists the agents the office publishes, and picks an image agent by capability rather than a fixed id. It runs the MaluOS task protocol, polling while the task works, and takes the first image artifact of the answer.
- **The `office_picture` tool** in the shared table, so the assistant, the HTTP API and MCP all have it. It moves to the slide asked for and inserts the bytes through the engine's picture command, so confirm mode shows it as a plan and undo removes it as one step.
- **Nothing from the web.** An artifact given by URL is read only under the office's own URL. When the desk is not enrolled or the office has no image agent, the tool says so and the instructions tell the model to look nowhere else.
- **A recipe and a quick action.** The instructions explain how to write the picture prompt and check placement. The pane gains "Add a picture".

**Verification.** Nine new tests run against a mock office over TCP, a mock vault over a Unix socket, and the mock model. The full workspace passes, along with clippy, format, assets, layers and the wasm check. Two live runs through the Ollama cloud model against the shipped mock office with an illustrator agent patched in:

- The CLI inserted the picture in four rounds. The rendered slide is in the status file.
- In the app, "Add a picture" in confirm mode produced a plan, I approved it, and the banner landed above the title with "Changed slide 1" and Undo in the pane. Screenshot linked from the status file.

**Your cross-application request.** I wrote `docs/maluos-slides/harness-design.md`. It holds thirty-two numbered decisions from all phases so far, each with why it was taken and what Malu123 and MaluDocs should mirror, including suggested quick actions and context outlines for a spreadsheet and a document editor. CLAUDE.md now requires a row there for every new decision, and I saved the instruction to memory.

**Still open on the platform side.** The real office's image agent and the artifact shape are ask 7 in the integration doc. The delegation envelope is adopted when it ships.

Next on the plan is 4.6, per-deck memory stored inside the file.

fn properties(s: &mut Session, p: &Value) -> Result<Value> {
    let fields = ["title", "subject", "author", "keywords", "comments", "category", "company"];
    if fields.iter().any(|f| p.get(*f).is_some()) {
        s.edit(|doc, _| {
            let pr = &mut doc.props;
            for f in fields {
                if let Some(v) = str_param(p, f) {
                    let slot = match f {
                        "title" => &mut pr.title,
                        "subject" => &mut pr.subject,
                        "author" => &mut pr.author,
                        "keywords" => &mut pr.keywords,
                        "comments" => &mut pr.comments,
                        "category" => &mut pr.category,
                        _ => &mut pr.company,
                    };
                    *slot = v.to_string();
                }
            }
            Ok(())
        })?;
    }
    Ok(serde_json::to_value(&s.doc()?.doc.props).unwrap_or_default())
}

fn revert(s: &mut Session, _p: &Value) -> Result<Value> {
    let st = s.doc_mut()?;
    st.doc = st.saved_doc.clone();
    st.history = crate::History { limit: st.history.limit, ..Default::default() };
    st.revision += 1;
    ok()
}

fn next_window(s: &mut Session, p: &Value) -> Result<Value> {
    let n = s.documents().len();
    if n == 0 {
        return ok();
    }
    let i = usize_param(p, "index").unwrap_or_else(|| (s.active_index().unwrap_or(0) + 1) % n);
    s.set_active(i.min(n - 1));
    ok()
}

pub fn show(app: &mut SlideApp, ui: &mut Ui) {
    if !app.malu.config_loaded {
        load_config(&mut app.malu);
    }
    let ctx = ui.ctx().clone();
    let t = Tokens::get(&ctx);
    poll(app, &ctx);
    if app.malu.send_requested {
        app.malu.send_requested = false;
        send(app, &ctx);
    }
    if let Some(v) = app.malu.verdict_requested.take()
        && app.malu.pending_plan.is_some()
    {
        answer_plan(app, &ctx, v);
    }

    settings_row(app, ui, &t);
    ui.add_space(4.0);
    let (ok, status) = app.malu.provider_status();
    ui.label(RichText::new(format!("{} · {}", app.malu.provider.label(), status)).small().color(if ok { t.text_dim } else { crate::icons::RED }));
    if let Some(p) = &app.malu.problem {
        ui.label(RichText::new(p).small().color(crate::icons::RED));
    }
    ui.add_space(6.0);

    // The conversation fills what the input box leaves.
    let input_h = 96.0;
    let avail = ui.available_height() - input_h;
    egui::ScrollArea::vertical().id_salt("malu_transcript").max_height(avail.max(80.0)).auto_shrink([false, false]).stick_to_bottom(true).show(
        ui,
        |ui| {
            transcript(app, ui, &ctx, &t);
        },
    );
    ui.add_space(6.0);
    quick_actions(app, ui, &ctx, &t);
    input_row(app, ui, &ctx, &t);
}

    pub provider: ProviderChoice,

    pub focus_input: bool,
    /// Show the model's reasoning under each answer.
    pub show_thinking: bool,
    /// The plan waiting for the user.
    pub pending_plan: Option<Plan>,
    /// Send the box's text on the next frame (`assist.ask {text, send: true}` from a script).
    pub send_requested: bool,
    /// Answer the waiting plan on the next frame (`assist.plan {verdict}` from a script).
    pub verdict_requested: Option<Verdict>,
    assistant: Option<Assistant>,
    custom_client: Option<Arc<dyn LlmClient>>,
    turn: Option<Turn>,
    worker: Option<Worker>,
    generation: u64,
    config_loaded: bool,
    config_dirty: bool,
    /// Why the last send could not start (no key, no model).
    pub problem: Option<String>,
}

    fn call(&mut self, method: &str, params: Value) -> Result<Value, String> {

            }
            "engine.commands" => Ok(serde_json::to_value(self.app.session.commands()).unwrap_or_default()),

#![allow(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::panic)]

use std::sync::Arc;
use std::time::Duration;

use serde_json::{Value, json};

use crate::malu_assistant::{self, Entry};
use crate::{Services, SlideApp};

fn calls(blocks: Vec<ContentBlock>) -> Completion {
    Completion {
        model: "mock".into(),
        content: blocks,
        stop_reason: StopReason::ToolUse,
        usage: Usage { input_tokens: 50, output_tokens: 5, cache_read_input_tokens: 0, cache_creation_input_tokens: 0 },
    }
}

fn answer(text: &str) -> Completion {
    Completion {
        model: "mock".into(),
        content: vec![ContentBlock::Text { text: text.into() }],
        stop_reason: StopReason::EndTurn,
        usage: Usage { input_tokens: 50, output_tokens: 5, cache_read_input_tokens: 0, cache_creation_input_tokens: 0 },
    }
}

fn tool_use(id: &str, name: &str, input: Value) -> ContentBlock {
    ContentBlock::ToolUse { id: id.into(), name: name.into(), input }
}

    app.malu.mode = mode;
    app.ui.pane = Some(malu_assistant::PANE.into());
    let mut h = Harness::builder().with_size(egui::vec2(1400.0, 900.0)).with_step_dt(1.0 / 60.0).build_ui_state(

fn a_quick_action_sends_its_request_for_the_current_slide() {
    let mock = Arc::new(MockClient::new());
    mock.push(calls(vec![tool_use("n", "run_command", json!({"command": "slide.notes", "params": {"text": "Start with the question."}}))]));
    mock.push(answer("Notes written."));
    let mut h = harness(mock.clone(), maluos_slides_assist::Mode::Autopilot);
    h.get_by_label("Write notes").click();
    h.run_steps(2);
    assert!(
        !h.state().malu.transcript.is_empty(),
        "nothing sent: input={:?} requested={} busy={}",
        h.state().malu.input,
        h.state().malu.send_requested,
        h.state().malu.busy()
    );
    settle(&mut h);
    assert_eq!(last_assistant(&h).0, "Notes written.");
    assert_eq!(h.state().session.active().unwrap().doc.slides[0].notes_text(), "Start with the question.");
    let sent = match &h.state().malu.transcript[0] {
        Entry::User(t) => t.clone(),
        other => panic!("{other:?}"),
    };
    assert!(sent.starts_with("Write speaker notes for this slide"), "{sent}");
    assert!(matches!(&mock.requests()[0].messages[0].content[0], ContentBlock::Text { text } if text == &sent));
}

Both formats round-trip tags, so the memory travels with the file, survives a\n//! save as PPTX and comes back when the deck is opened in another session or on another desk.\n//! Reading and writing go through the engine command `document.tags`, so a remembered note is\n//! an undoable change like any other and marks the deck dirty until saved.\n//!\n//! What belongs here: lasting facts about this deck (the audience, the tone, the time limit,\n//! what must not change, decisions taken). What never does: secrets, keys, anything about other\n//! decks or the user in general.\n\nuse maluos_slides_mcp::Backend;\nuse serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};\nuse serde_json::{Value, json};\n\n/// The tag that holds the memory.\npub const TAG: &str = \"maluos.assistant.memory\";\n/// Most notes kept; the oldest goes when a new one arrives past this.\npub const MAX_NOTES: usize = 24;\n/// Characters of one note; longer notes are cut with `…`.\npub const MAX_NOTE_CHARS: usize = 240;\n/// The JSON's `v`, for a later shape change.\npub const VERSION: u32 = 1;\n\n/// One remembered note.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub struct Note {\n    pub text: String,\n    /// The day it was written, `YYYY-MM-DD` (UTC).\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub when: String,\n}\n\n/// The notes of one deck.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub struct DeckMemory {\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub notes: Vec<Note>,\n}\n\nimpl DeckMemory {\n    /// From the presentation's tags: the memory tag parsed, or empty when absent or unreadable.\n    pub fn from_tags(tags: &[(String, String)]) -> DeckMemory {\n        tags.iter().find(|(n, _)| n == TAG).map(|(_, v)| Self::from_tag_value(v)).unwrap_or_default()\n    }\n\n    /// From the tag's value.\n    pub fn from_tag_value(value: &str) -> DeckMemory {\n        serde_json::from_str::<Value>(value)\n            .ok()\n            .and_then(|v| serde_json::from_value::<DeckMemory>(v.get(\"memory\").cloned().unwrap_or(v)).ok())\n            .unwrap_or_default()\n    }\n\n    /// The tag's value.\n    pub fn to_tag_value(&self) -> String {\n        json!({\"v\": VERSION, \"memory\": self}).to_string()\n    }\n\n    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {\n        self.notes.is_empty()\n    }\n\n    /// Add a note (trimmed, cut at [`MAX_NOTE_CHARS`]); a note already there (case-insensitive)\n    /// is not added twice. Past [`MAX_NOTES`] the oldest goes. Returns the note's index.\n    pub fn remember(&mut self, text: &str, when: &str) -> Result<usize, String> {\n        let text = cut(text.split_whitespace().collect::<Vec<_>>().join(\" \").as_str(), MAX_NOTE_CHARS);\n        if text.is_empty() {\n            return Err(\"remember: the note is empty\".into());\n        }\n        if let Some(i) = self.notes.iter().position(|n| n.text.eq_ignore_ascii_case(&text)) {\n            return Ok(i);\n        }\n        self.notes.push(Note { text, when: when.into() });\n        while self.notes.len() > MAX_NOTES {\n            self.notes.remove(0);\n        }\n        Ok(self.notes.len() - 1)\n    }\n\n    /// Drop the note at `index`.\n    pub fn forget(&mut self, index: usize) -> Option<Note> {\n        (index < self.notes.len()).then(|| self.notes.remove(index))\n    }\n\n    /// The notes as the prompt shows them: one line each, numbered from 0 for `forget`.\n    pub fn lines(&self) -> String {\n        let mut s = String::new();\n        for (i, n) in self.notes.iter().enumerate() {\n            s.push_str(&format!(\"- [{i}] {}{}\\n\", n.text, if n.when.is_empty() { String::new() } else { format!(\" ({})\", n.when) }));\n        }\n        s\n    }\n\n    /// The `document.tags` params that store this memory (or remove the tag when empty).\n    pub fn tag_params(&self) -> Value {\n        if self.is_empty() { json!({\"remove\": [TAG]}) } else { json!({\"set\": {TAG: self.to_tag_value()}}) }\n    }\n}\n\nfn cut(s: &str, max: usize) -> String {\n    if s.chars().count() <= max { s.to_string() } else { s.chars().take(max - 1).collect::<String>() + \"…\" }\n}\n\n/// Today as `YYYY-MM-DD` (UTC), without a calendar crate.\npub fn today() -> String {\n    let secs = std::time::SystemTime::now().duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH).map(|d| d.as_secs()).unwrap_or(0);\n    let days = (secs / 86_400) as i64;\n    // Howard Hinnant's civil-from-days.\n    let z = days + 719_468;\n    let era = z.div_euclid(146_097);\n    let doe = z.rem_euclid(146_097);\n    let yoe = (doe - doe / 1460 + doe / 36_524 - doe / 146_096) / 365;\n    let y = yoe + era * 400;\n    let doy = doe - (365 * yoe + yoe / 4 - yoe / 100);\n    let mp = (5 * doy + 2) / 153;\n    let d = doy - (153 * mp + 2) / 5 + 1;\n    let m = if mp < 10 { mp + 3 } else { mp - 9 };\n    let y = if m <= 2 { y + 1 } else { y };\n    format!(\"{y:04}-{m:02}-{d:02}\")\n}\n\n/// The memory of the backend's presentation, read through `document.tags`.\npub fn read(backend: &mut dyn Backend) -> Result<DeckMemory, String> {\n    let v = backend.call(\"engine.execute\", json!({\"command\": \"document.tags\", \"params\": {}}))?;\n    Ok(v.pointer(&format!(\"/tags/{TAG}\")).and_then(Value::as_str).map(DeckMemory::from_tag_value).unwrap_or_default())\n}\n\n/// Store `memory` through `document.tags` (one undoable change).\npub fn write(backend: &mut dyn Backend, memory: &DeckMemory) -> Result<(), String> {\n    backend.call(\"engine.execute\", json!({\"command\": \"document.tags\", \"params\": memory.tag_params()})).map(|_| ())\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod unit {\n    #![allow(clippy::unwrap_used)]\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn notes_round_trip_dedupe_and_cap() {\n        let mut m = DeckMemory::default();\n        assert_eq!(m.remember(\"  The audience is   the board. \", \"2026-11-03\"), Ok(0));\n        assert_eq!(m.remember(\"the audience is the board.\", \"2026-11-04\"), Ok(0), \"same note, once\");\n        assert_eq!(m.remember(\"Keep it under ten minutes\", \"2026-11-03\"), Ok(1));\n        assert!(m.remember(\"   \", \"x\").is_err());\n        let back = DeckMemory::from_tag_value(&m.to_tag_value());\n        assert_eq!(back, m);\n        assert_eq!(back.lines(), \"- [0] The audience is the board. (2026-11-03)\\n- [1] Keep it under ten minutes (2026-11-03)\\n\");\n        assert_eq!(DeckMemory::from_tags(&[(\"other\".into(), \"x\".into()), (TAG.into(), m.to_tag_value())]), m);\n        assert!(DeckMemory::from_tag_value(\"not json\").is_empty());\n        assert!(DeckMemory::from_tags(&[]).is_empty());\n        assert_eq!(m.forget(0).map(|n| n.text), Some(\"The audience is the board.\".into()));\n        assert_eq!(m.forget(5), None);\n        assert_eq!(m.notes.len(), 1);\n        for i in 0..40 {\n            m.remember(&format!(\"note {i}\"), \"d\").unwrap();\n        }\n        assert_eq!(m.notes.len(), MAX_NOTES);\n        assert_eq!(m.notes[0].text, format!(\"note {}\", 40 - MAX_NOTES));\n        let long = \"x\".repeat(400);\n        let i = m.remember(&long, \"d\").unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(m.notes[i].text.chars().count(), MAX_NOTE_CHARS);\n        assert!(m.notes[i].text.ends_with('…'));\n        assert_eq!(DeckMemory::default().tag_params(), json!({\"remove\": [TAG]}));\n        assert!(m.tag_params()[\"set\"][TAG].is_string());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn today_is_a_date() {\n        let t = today();\n        assert_eq!(t.len(), 10);\n        assert!(t.starts_with(\"20\"), \"{t}\");\n        assert_eq!(&t[4..5], \"-\");\n    }\n}\n"

        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("maluos-slides-write-file-{}-{name}", std::process::id()));
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
        dir
    }

    #[test]
    fn write_file_does_not_touch_a_predictable_saving_sibling() {
        let dir = scratch("sibling");
        let dest = dir.join("deck.deckcraft");
        let dest_str = dest.to_str().unwrap();
        std::fs::write(&dest, b"old").unwrap();
        std::fs::write(dir.join("deck.deckcraft.saving"), b"precious").unwrap();
        write_file(dest_str, b"new").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(std::fs::read(&dest).unwrap(), b"new");
        assert_eq!(std::fs::read(dir.join("deck.deckcraft.saving")).unwrap(), b"precious");
        let names: Vec<_> = std::fs::read_dir(&dir).unwrap().map(|e| e.unwrap().file_name()).collect();
        assert_eq!(names.len(), 2, "no temporary file may be left behind: {names:?}");
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
    }

    #[test]
    fn write_file_failed_rename_keeps_destination_and_cleans_up() {
        let dir = scratch("failed");
        let dest = dir.join("target");
        std::fs::create_dir(&dest).unwrap();
        assert!(write_file(dest.to_str().unwrap(), b"new").is_err());
        assert!(dest.is_dir());
        assert_eq!(std::fs::read_dir(&dir).unwrap().count(), 1);
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
        assert!(dest.is_dir());
        assert_eq!(std::fs::read_dir(&dir).unwrap().count(), 1);
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
    }
}

## 🤖 Claude

Phase 4.6 is done, committed as `77ea5c12` and pushed. With it, Phase 4 is complete apart from 4.3, which you deferred.

**What landed.**

- **Memory inside the deck.** The assistant's notes about a deck live in one presentation-level add-in tag, a small versioned JSON of dated notes. Both file formats already round-trip these tags, so nothing changed in the formats and the notes travel with the file, including through a save as PPTX.
- **One engine command.** The assistant may only write through commands and none existed for tags, so I added `document.tags` to the engine, written the way upstream would and worth sending to them. This is the first fork addition inside an upstream crate. I recorded it as decision H33 in the design record and in the status file, so the exception is explicit.
- **Three tools** in the shared table: remember, forget by index or all, and recall. A remembered note is one undoable change that marks the deck dirty until saved. Notes are trimmed, capped at 240 characters and 24 entries, and never stored twice.
- **The model sees them** under "Remembered about this deck" in every later session, with the instructions saying what belongs there and that secrets never do. **The pane** shows "Remembered (N)" with a Forget button per note.

**Verification.** New tests cover the engine command with undo and a round trip through PPTX and native bytes, the tools, the next turn's prompt, and the pane. The workspace passes along with clippy, format, assets, layers and the wasm check.

**Live runs** with the Ollama cloud model:

- The CLI stored "for the executive board, ten minutes" into a PPTX. A fresh session opened that file, recalled the note with its date, and checked the deck against the limit using the timing tool.
- In the app, the same request in confirm mode made a plan. After approval the pane shows Remembered (1) and the tag reads back through the control channel. Screenshot linked from the status file.

**Design record.** H33 and H34 are added to `docs/maluos-slides/harness-design.md`, including where Malu123 and MaluDocs should keep their per-document memory.

**What remains on the plan.** Step 4.3 waits on the MaluDB query path. Phase 5 is parity through weekly upstream merges and sending our fixes upstream, which now include the stale-id slide delete fix and `document.tags`. The platform asks in the integration doc are still open, chiefly the vault key source for cloud providers and the office's image agent.

# The rename: DeckCraft to MaluOS Slides

> **Created:** 2026-10-24 · plan step 2.4

Every crate, binary and identifier is renamed, not only the apps (decision D2 in
[plan.md](plan.md)). One script holds the whole mapping, `scripts/rename-upstream.sh` (what the
fork drops, path moves, `cargo fmt`) with the text rules in `scripts/rename-upstream.py`
(`--list` prints them). It is idempotent.

## Mapping

| Upstream | MaluOS Slides | Where |
|---|---|---|
| `deckcraft-geom`, `deckcraft-engine`, … | `maluos-slides-geom`, `maluos-slides-engine`, … | crate names, `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` |
| `deckcraft_geom::`, … | `maluos_slides_geom::`, … | Rust paths |
| `deckcraft`, `deckcraft-cli`, `deckcraft-web` | `maluos-slides`, `maluos-slides-cli`, `maluos-slides-web` | packages, binaries, `apps/` directories |
| `ai.storyteller.deckcraft`, developer id `ai.storyteller` | `org.maluos.slides`, `org.maluos` | app id: desktop file, metainfo, MIME, flatpak manifest, icon file names, `StartupWMClass` |
| `DECKCRAFT_*` | `MALUOS_SLIDES_*` | environment variables (`MALUOS_SLIDES_NO_PREFS`, `MALUOS_SLIDES_SOAK_STEPS`, `MALUOS_SLIDES_BUILD_SHA`, …) |
| `DeckCraft` | `MaluOS Slides` | product name: window title, About, metainfo, PPTX `<Application>`, PDF producer, MCP server title |
| `deckcraft` as a log target (`warn,deckcraft*=info`, `"deckcraft::audio"`) | `maluos_slides` | the desktop binary's crate path has an underscore; `apps/maluos-slides/src/logging.rs` |
| `deckcraft://commands` | `maluos-slides://commands` | MCP resource URIs; MCP `serverInfo.name` is `maluos-slides` |
| `~/.
```

<details><summary>🔧 tool result</summary>

```
rename-upstream.py
rename-upstream.sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# DeckCraft -> MaluOS Slides. The single source of the name mapping (docs/maluos-slides/rename.md).
#
# Run from the repository root on a clean tree. Idempotent. Does, in order:
#   1. removes what the fork drops: upstream's ArtCraft brand files (their licence requires it of
#      forks), the macOS, Windows and FreeBSD packaging and icons (two metadata files stay as
#      test fixtures), upstream's workflows and the
#      configs of services the fork does not use (decision D1 in docs/maluos-slides/plan.md)
#   2. git-moves every tracked path whose name contains "deckcraft" (app id first; the native
#      format extension `.deckcraft` stays)
#   3. rewrites the text of every tracked file with scripts/rename-upstream.py
#   4. cargo fmt (longer identifiers make rustfmt rewrap lines) and re-sorts Cargo.lock
#
# Upstream sync (vendor branch): on `upstream-renamed`, `git merge upstream/main`, resolve any
# conflicts by re-running this script, commit, then `git merge upstream-renamed` on main.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

# Files this script never rewrites: they describe the fork itself.
SKIP='^(README\.md|LICENSE-MIT|LICENSE-APACHE|docs/maluos-slides/.*|scripts/rename-upstream\..*|\.github/workflows/maluos-.*)$'

# 1. what the fork drops
# (`packaging/macos/Info.plist.in` and `packaging/windows/deckcraft.wxs` stay: the desktop app's test
# `every_desktop_offers_the_same_file_types` reads them as fixtures; they are not built.)
git ls-files packaging/macos packaging/windows | grep -vE '^packaging/(macos/Info\.plist\.in|windows/(deckcraft|maluos-slides)\.wxs)$' | xargs -r -d '\n' git rm -q
git rm -rq --ignore-unmatch \
  docs/brand \
  packaging/freebsd packaging/icons.sh \
  assets/app-icon/deckcraft.icns assets/app-icon/deckcraft.ico \
  .github/workflows/ci.yml .github/workflows/release.yml .github/workflows/packaging-lint.yml \
  .github/workflows/freebsd.yml .github/workflows/nix.yml .github/workflows/sonarcloud.yml \
  .github/workflows/windows-arm64.yml \
  .github/dependabot.yml .coderabbit.yaml sonar-project.properties omastore.toml
# ATTRIBUTION rows of the removed assets, and the three places that call the brand files "the one exception"
sed -i -e '/^| `docs\/brand\//d' -e '/^| `packaging\/macos\//d' -e '/^| `assets\/app-icon\/deckcraft\.icns`/d' ATTRIBUTION.md
sed -i 's/fails if a file under `assets\/`, `docs\/images\/` or `docs\/brand\/` is missing from this table\./fails if a file under `assets\/` or `docs\/images\/` is missing from this table. The ArtCraft brand files of upstream DeckCraft (`docs\/brand\/`) are trademarks and are removed from this fork, as their licence requires./' ATTRIBUTION.md
python3 - <<'EOF'
import re
p = "AGENTS.md"
s = open(p).read()
s = re.sub(r"One narrow exception: the ArtCraft name, wordmark and logos in `docs/brand/` are trademarks of the\nArtCraft Team \(not open source, terms in `docs/brand/LICENSE-brand.txt`\), used only unmodified to\nidentify the project\.",
           "The ArtCraft brand files of upstream DeckCraft (`docs/brand/`) are trademarks and are removed from\nthis fork, as their licence requires; upstream DeckCraft is credited in the About box and the README.", s)
s = s.replace("fails if a file under `assets/`, `docs/images/`\n  or `docs/brand/` has no row.", "fails if a file under `assets/` or `docs/images/`\n  has no row.")
open(p, "w").write(s)
p = "NOTICE"
s = open(p).read()
s = re.sub(r"The ArtCraft name, wordmark and logos in docs/brand/ are trademarks of the ArtCraft Team\. They are\nnot open source and are not covered by the license above; their terms are in\ndocs/brand/LICENSE-brand\.txt\.",
           "MaluOS Slides is a fork of DeckCraft. The ArtCraft name, wordmark and logos are trademarks of the\nArtCraft Team; upstream's brand files (docs/brand/) are not included in this fork, as their\nlicence requires. MaluOS additions are Copyright (c) 2026 MaluOS, under the same licenses
```
