## 🤖 Claude

Phase 5 is under way: the first upstream sync is merged, verified and pushed, and the two upstream-bound fixes are ready as patches. Commits `b4153065`, `2aeee42a` and `50d507e5` on main, plus the vendor branch.

**The sync.** Upstream moved 761 commits since the rename base, touching 497 files, including a split of the window crate's big files into modules and a move to egui 0.37 with their own widget crate.

- **Vendor branch.** 102 conflicts, every one resolved toward upstream since that branch holds nothing but the rename, then the rename script. Four script fixes came out of it: forced removal of dropped files a merge leaves staged, a count that no longer fails under pipefail, protection of an external crate's constant, and keeping the Windows package script as a test fixture.
- **Main.** 8 conflicts. Every fenced hook moved to its new home in upstream's layout: the pane dispatch, the title-bar button, the presenter hints, the icon, the commands and the frame poll. Fork code adapted to upstream's lint rules and API drift: the disallowed combo box, a deprecated id call, accessible names on the pane's combos, the CLI's automation roots, a complexity threshold on tests. Two snapshots regenerated.
- **Cost.** About 45 minutes including the gates. It is written up in `docs/maluos-slides/rename.md` with the procedure, and the plan's step 2.9 is closed.

**Verification.** All gates pass on the merged tree. One upstream test fails here because this host has no Korean font, which is environment, not code. The pdf font test that used to fail now passes. The app runs on your desktop at upstream's 0.15.0 with the Malu pane answering a timing question, screenshot linked from the status file.

**Sending fixes upstream.** Two patches in upstream's naming are ready and apply cleanly to their main:

MaluOS Slides is a fork of [DeckCraft](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft), the open-source,
clean-room presentation app by the ArtCraft team. It keeps DeckCraft's engine, renderer, PPTX
support and agent surface, and adds the MaluOS fit: a MaluOS package, the MaluOS desktop, and, step
by step, an LLM assistant that works through the MaluOS gateway. Upstream is tracked as the
`upstream` remote and merged regularly; the plan is in
[`docs/maluos-slides/plan.md`](docs/maluos-slides/plan.md) and progress in
[`docs/maluos-slides/status.md`](docs/maluos-slides/status.md).

MaluOS Slides work is planned in [`docs/maluos-slides/plan.md`](docs/maluos-slides/plan.md).
Feature parity with PowerPoint is upstream's work, tracked in [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md),
[`docs/target-app-parity.md`](docs/target-app-parity.md) and [`docs/gaps.md`](docs/gaps.md); we
merge it rather than redo it, and send fixes upstream.

## 🤖 Claude

Done, recorded as owner decision D12 and pushed as `583cd7a5`. No pull requests were or will be opened.

**What I did.**

- Removed the `upstream` remote and the local vendor branch. The two patches prepared for upstream are deleted.
- Checked GitHub: `maludb/maluos-slides` is not registered as a fork there, so no "forked from" link exists to detach.
- Rewrote the rules. CLAUDE.md no longer says "keep upstream mergeable". It says keep the layering: MaluOS features stay in their own crates and fenced hooks, but inherited crates may now be edited directly when a feature needs it. The design record's H1 says the same, for Malu123 and MaluDocs.
- Rewrote Phase 5 in the plan as independent evolution. The inherited roadmap and parity documents are ours to pursue or prune. D7, the weekly sync, is retired. The rename doc's sync procedure is marked history.
- README and status say the app is developed independently since today.
- Saved the decision to memory so I never propose upstream PRs or syncs again.

**What stays, deliberately.** DeckCraft remains credited in the licence files, NOTICE, the About box and the README. The MIT and Apache licences require the copyright notices to stay, and the credit is the honest record. The `.deckcraft` format name and ids stay for file compatibility, per decision D3.

**One thing I could not do.** The vendor branch still exists on GitHub. Deleting a remote branch is classed as destructive and was blocked. If you want it gone, run this in a terminal:

```
git push origin --delete upstream-renamed
```

**Remaining ties to storytold's other repositories.** The build still pulls craft-fonts, craft-libs and their egui fork, pinned by revision in Cargo.lock, so it keeps building as is. Vendoring those is a later decision if they move or disappear. I noted that in the plan.

The local backup branch `backup/pre-p5-sync` from before the merge is still here and unpushed. It can go whenever you like.

### Phase 5: independent evolution (was: parity through upstream)

One sync was done (2026-11-03, upstream `aa13eeb4`, measured in rename.md). Then the owner
decided (D12) to cut the link: no upstream remote, no vendor branch, no merges, no pull
requests to storytold/deckcraft. The inherited roadmap (ROADMAP.md, `docs/target-app-parity.md`,
`docs/gaps.md`) is ours to pursue or prune; parity work is planned here as steps like any other.
Remaining dependencies on storytold's other repositories (craft-fonts, craft-libs, their egui
fork, pinned by revision in Cargo.lock) keep building as pinned; vendoring them is a later
decision if they move or vanish.

## Repository conventions

- `docs/maluos-slides/` holds everything fork-specific: this plan, `status.md`, `rename.md`,
  later `llm.md`, `assistant.md`, `packaging.md`. Upstream docs stay as they are.
- Commits: one step id per commit (`P2.4: scripted rename, vendor branch`), co-author lines as the
  MaluOS repos use them. Branches: `main` is ours; `upstream-renamed` is the vendor branch; merges
  land as merge commits.
- Quality gate before every push: `cargo xtask ci`. New crates carry upstream's clippy denies
  (`unwrap_used`, `expect_used`, `panic`, `todo`, `unreachable`).
- Build on the dev host (the owner's MaluOS desktop) under `systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryHigh=4500M -p MemoryMax=6G` with
  `-j 6`; the recipe is in status.md.
- Never commit: fonts, PowerPoint-authored files, screenshots of Microsoft software, API keys,
  `dist/`, `target/`.

# Where MaluOS Slides falls short of PowerPoint

> **Last reviewed:** 2026-10-30 · **Last updated:** 2026-11-03 · **Change:** trivial (run alternate language and reflection transforms survive saves; reused slide contents scale to the destination, pi

PowerPoint from switching. This is the work list: pick from the top. Numbers are summarized in
[target-app-parity.md](target-app-parity.md); the feature-by-feature scores are in
[parity-checklist.md](parity-checklist.md). Hours are Opus 5.5 agent wall-clock hours including
tests (calibration in [target-app-parity.md](target-app-parity.md#calibration-how-the-hours-were-derived)).

[alpha gate](roadmap.md#alpha-gate-powerpoints-core-workflows).

revision history.

## 🤖 Claude

Here is where the plan stands and what I recommend next.

**Already resolved since my last message.** The vendor branch is gone from GitHub, so the only remaining remote branches are `main` and one dependabot branch. Every assistant step in Phases 3 and 4 is done except 4.3, which is deferred on the platform.

**Open work, in the order I would take it.**

1. **Housekeeping after the cut, about an hour.** The README still shows the DeckCraft icon path, which is a broken image on GitHub, says the rename has not landed, uses the old `deckcraft-cli` command names, and refers to the dev VM. The status file header still lists the upstream remote and says upstream code is untouched. The 2.5 row says "planned" although the rename already delivered the app id, desktop entry and a placeholder icon. One commit fixes all of that.
2. **Phase 2 remainder, ship it on MaluOS (2.6, 2.7, 2.8).** The app runs on your desk from a local build, but it is not in the MaluOS archive or on the desktop image yet. 2.6 is the vendored deb and the grid entry per decision D8, 2.7 is the boot test on the desktop ISO, 2.8 applies the fonts decision D5. Together roughly 6 to 11 hours. The only open piece of 2.5 is a real icon in place of the placeholder.
3. **Prune the inherited roadmap, now that it is ours (Phase 5).** The gaps list still ranks Windows paste and other non-Linux items. A pass that drops those and re-ranks for MaluOS gives a work list. The top candidates relevant to your desk are the stability items, SVG pictures not rendering, printing, and presenter view on the second display.
4. **API loose ends from 3.8.** The HTTP API is not served from inside the running app, has no streaming ask and no conversation ids. These matter once Malu123 or MaluDocs call Slides.
5. **Platform-blocked items.** 4.3 data slides wait on a MaluDB query path for desktop apps. The office image agent is ask 7. The vault key source and gateway provider asks are still open on the MaluOS side. Nothing to do here until the platform answers.
6. **The second app.** The design record is ready for Malu123. Decision D6 says the shared `maluos-llm` crate moves to its own repository when a second app consumes it. That extraction is the first step of the Malu123 work, not of Slides.

**My recommendation** is 1 then 2. The assistant is feature-complete for the plan, so the most valuable next move is getting the product installed the MaluOS way and boot-tested, with the docs truthful first. Say "start housekeeping" or "start 2.6" and I will go.

Two things still running on your desk from the live checks: the two mock office user units on ports 18080 and 18081, and a debug app instance with control port 7990. I will stop them when you confirm you do not need them.

==== vendor script
#!/bin/bash
# Replace vendor/malu123/*.deb with the Malu123 packages found in <dir> (output of
# packaging/linux/package.sh and packaging/web/deb.sh in the malu123 repo) and update the README table.
set -euo pipefail
ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd); SRC=${1:?usage: $0 <dir-with-debs>}
rm -f "$ROOT"/vendor/malu123/*.deb
cp "$SRC"/malu123-*-linux-x86_64.deb "$SRC"/malu123-web_*_all.deb "$ROOT/vendor/malu123/"
for d in "$ROOT"/vendor/malu123/*.deb; do
    p=$(dpkg-deb -f "$d" Package); v=$(dpkg-deb -f "$d" Version)
    sha=$(sha256sum "$d" | cut -c1-16)
    sed -i "s/^| $p | .* |$/| $p | $v | $sha… |/" "$ROOT/vendor/malu123/README.md"
done
ls -1 "$ROOT"/vendor/malu123/*.deb
==== vendor README
# Vendored Malu123 package

Malu123 is the MaluOS spreadsheet: Excel-compatible, native, with an LLM assistant on the way.
It is built from [maludb/malu123](https://github.com/maludb/malu123), a fork of GridCraft
(MIT OR Apache-2.0). The binary package is carried here so that the repository, image and CI
builds are self-contained; a Rust toolchain is not needed to build MaluOS. Refresh with
`scripts/vendor-malu123-deb.sh <dir-with-debs>` after `packaging/linux/package.sh` in the
malu123 checkout; both local publishing (repo/publish.sh) and CI pick it up from this directory.
The desktop seed depends on `malu123`, so every desktop image installs it. `malu123-web` is the
browser build (WebAssembly, a static site under `/usr/share/malu123-web`) that enables `/malu123/`
on Apache where it is installed; the business-os seed recommends it, so the server edition serves
the spreadsheet to every browser on the office network.

#!/bin/bash
# Generate packages/maluos-meta/debian/control from seeds/*.seed.
set -euo pipefail
ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
META=$ROOT/packages/maluos-meta/debian
OUT=$META/control

cp "$META/control.head" "$OUT"
for seed in "$ROOT"/seeds/*.seed; do
    name=$(basename "$seed" .seed)
    deps=(); recs=()
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        line=${line%%#*}; line=$(echo "$line" | xargs)
        [ -z "$line" ] && continue
        case "$line" in
            \?*) recs+=("${line#?}") ;;
            *)   deps+=("$line") ;;
        esac
    done < "$seed"
    IFS='|' read -r _ synopsis long < <(grep "^$name|" "$META/descriptions") \

server|MaluOS memory server|A headless MaluOS memory host: PostgreSQL 18 with the MaluDB memory core extension and the MC2DB MCP listener.

business-os|MaluDB Business OS kernel|The MaluDB Business OS kernel: the estate, departments and people, the AI agent workforce, single sign-on and the directory API for business applications, approvals and AI Ops, with MaluDB as activity memory. Provisioned on first boot.
desktop|MaluOS desktop workstation (GNOME)|The MaluOS workstation: GNOME with the Ubuntu session extensions and the Yaru look, the MaluOS identity on the login screen and the desktop, Firefox from Mozilla's repository and GNOME Software with the deb plugin only (no snaps). Install beside maluos-server for a workstation that is also a memory host. With maluos-desk the workstation enrols as a desk of a Business OS office (maluctl office): the office's models through the desk's gateway, its endpoints for the agents here, and presence in the office's estate while the person is signed in.
live|MaluOS live environment (the installer medium)|The live environment the MaluOS installer medium boots into: a server-minimal MaluOS with casper, the installer, NetworkManager on a console, and the disk and hardware tools an install needs. Never installed on a target.
apple-t2|Apple T2 Mac support|The drivers and daemons an Intel Mac with the T2 chip (2018 and later) needs: the T2 bridge driver for the internal keyboard, trackpad, Touch Bar, camera and audio, the SMC and trackpad drivers patched for the T2, the Touch Bar function row and the fan daemon, the audio profiles, the Wi-Fi and Bluetooth firmware import from the Mac's own macOS, and Vulkan for the Radeon. The installer selects it on a T2 Mac.
nvidia|NVIDIA GPU driver for an RTX card|The NVIDIA driver for an RTX card in a MaluOS box: the Canonical-signed kernel modules for the generic kernel (no DKMS build, Secure Boot without MOK enrolment), the 595 driver branch with 580 as the alternative, nvidia-smi for `maluctl gpu status` and the System Monitor's GPUs tab, and nvtop as a recommend. Ollama finds the GPU on its own. A DGX Spark is arm64 and is not a MaluOS device; an RTX card in an x86 box is the MaluOS case.

---- readme

## Layout

```
packages/      source packages owned by MaluOS (keyring, archive, metapackages,
               branding, first boot + maluctl, vault, inference gateway, agents,
               the desktop session service + shell extension, vendored components)
seeds/         package lists per variant; metapackage Depends are generated from these
repo/          aptly configuration and publish scripts
scripts/       build helpers and the client bootstrap installer
tests/         install tests (clean mmdebstrap chroot), image boot tests,
               vault and gateway harnesses (tests/vault-local-test.sh,
               tests/gateway-local-test.sh: no VM, no GPU needed)
ci/            CI build scripts (flat repo, in-container build); workflows in .github/
autoinstall/   subiquity autoinstall templates             (Phase 2+)
firstboot/     first-boot provisioning                      (Phase 4)
  squashfs and qcow2 are built in a privileged ubuntu:26.04 container from an
  unsigned flat repo (no signing key in CI), then the qcow2 is boot-tested on
  BIOS and UEFI with KVM and uploaded. The manual run can also build the ISO
  and the desktop image (input `desktop`).
- The MaluDB engine packages come from vendor/maludb/ (see its README).

## Quick start (client)

```
curl -fsSL https://apt.maluos.com/bootstrap/install-maluos.sh | sudo bash
```

## 🤖 Claude

Housekeeping and step 2.6 are done and pushed. Both repositories are level with GitHub, and the full gate passed with all 8 steps green.

**Housekeeping, commit `3fb7e520`.** The README now shows the real icon, drops the "until the rename lands" note, uses the maluos-slides command names, links the assistant, CLI and API docs, and names the MaluOS archive as the install path. The status header says the app is independent since today with origin as the only remote. Step 2.5 is recorded as mostly done by the rename, with only the designed icon still open.

**Step 2.6, commit `4eb91bf6` here and `a2456dc` in maludb/maluos.** The MaluOS repository now carries the Slides package the same way it carries Malu123:

- `vendor/maluos-slides/` holds the 0.15.0 deb and a README table with version and checksum.
- `scripts/vendor-maluos-slides-deb.sh` refreshes it from a Slides build.
- `seeds/desktop.seed` lists `maluos-slides`, so the desktop metapackage depends on it and every desktop image installs it. The metapackage changelog is at 0.2.15.
- The next publish run picks it up, since the publish script and the CI flat repo take every vendored deb.

The pattern is recorded as design-record row H35 for Malu123 and MaluDocs.

**Two things I had to fix along the way.**

- The release build failed because the fonts crate, since the upstream sync, requires craft-fonts' simplified-Chinese manifest when fonts are required. I moved the craft-fonts checkout to its current main, and the build passed. The Korean composing tests pass now too.
- The gzip deb was 107 MB, over GitHub's hard limit of 100 MiB per file. Both binaries embed 80 MB of fonts. Switching the deb to xz compression brought it to 88 MB, which pushed fine with only the usual large-file warning.

**Two items need you.**

1. The workflow pin to the new craft-fonts commit sits uncommitted in `.github/workflows/maluos-ci.yml` and `maluos-release.yml`. GitHub refuses workflow edits from the current token. Run this once, then commit and push those two files:

```
gh auth refresh -h github.com -s workflow
```

2. Installing the package on this desk needs sudo:

```
sudo apt install ./dist/release/maluos-slides-0.15.0-linux-x86_64.deb
```

**What is next.** Step 2.7 is the boot test on the desktop image, and 2.8 is the fonts decision. The size measurement makes 2.8 concrete: the fonts crate can load a directory at run time, so a shared `maluos-fonts` package would carry the 80 MB once for Slides, Malu123 and MaluDocs, and shrink the Slides deb to roughly a quarter of its size. The two mock office units and the debug app instance are still running on your desk, and I will stop them when you say so.

            .iter()

            .map(|f| (f.italic, f.weight, f.style.clone()))
            .collect();
        #[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]
        for c in self.read_catalog().iter() {
            if c.family.eq_ignore_ascii_case(family) && !v.iter().any(|(_, _, s)| s.eq_ignore_ascii_case(&c.style)) {
                v.push((style_italic(&c.style), style_weight(&c.style), c.style.clone()));

install -Dm755 "$BIN/maluos-slides-cli" "$STAGE/usr/bin/maluos-slides-cli"
"${CROSS_COMPILE:-}strip" "$STAGE/usr/bin/maluos-s

```
/// Does `face` draw every character of the cluster?
pub fn covers_cluster(face: &FontFace, cluster: &[char]) -> bool {
    cluster.iter().all(|c| ignorable(*c) || face.covers(*c))
}

/// Installed families tried by name for a script after the bundled face, before scanning every
/// installed font. Microsoft font names are not listed (AGENTS.md §1.1); an installed one is
/// still used by the scan when nothing earlier covers the cluster.
fn os_families(script: ScriptTag) -> &'static [&'static str] {
    match &script {
        b"Arab" => &["Noto Naskh Arabic", "Noto Sans Arabic", "Geeza Pro", "SF Arabic", "DejaVu Sans"],
        b"Hebr" => &["Noto Sans Hebrew", "Arial Hebrew", "SF Hebrew", "DejaVu Sans"],
        b"Thai" => &["Noto Sans Thai", "Thonburi"],
        b"Deva" => &["Noto Sans Devanagari", "Kohinoor Devanagari", "Devanagari Sangam MN"],
        _ => &[],
    }
}

/// The craft-fonts families for a script (manifest order), e.g. Noto Naskh Arabic for `Arab`.
pub fn bundled_families(script: ScriptTag) -> Vec<&'static str> {
    let tag = std::str::from_utf8(&script).unwrap_or("");
    let mut v: Vec<&'static str> = CRAFT_FONTS.iter().filter(|f| f.scripts.contains(&tag)).map(|f| f.family).collect();
    v.dedup();
    v
}

impl FontDb {
    /// The face for one grapheme cluster: the first of `chain` that draws all of it, else the
    /// bundled face for its script, else an installed face for the script, else any loaded

//! MaluOS Slides fonts: the font database (craft-fonts families, user and system fonts, and open
//! substitutes for the Office fonts presentations ask for), vertical metrics, glyph outlines and
//! OpenType shaping, script/slot classification and per-cluster fallback.
//!
//! Shaping here is style-agnostic: [`shape`] and [`shape_range`] turn text in one face into glyph
//! ids, clusters and advances in font units. `maluos-slides-text` applies sizes, tracking, scaling and
//! justification on top.
#![deny(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::panic, clippy::unimplemented, clippy::todo, clippy::unreachable)]

    system_font_dirs,
};
pub use harfrust::Feature;

pub use kurbo::BezPath;

/// A font from the optional craft-fonts build input (https://github.com/storytold/craft-fonts;
/// empty unless built with `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR`, see `build.rs`).
pub struct CraftFont {
    pub family: &'static str,
    pub style: &'static str,
    /// ISO 15924 scripts the font is for, e.g. `"Jpan"`.
    pub scripts: &'static [&'static str],
    pub bytes: &'static [u8],
}

/// The craft-fonts faces for Japanese (`"Jpan"`), in manifest order. Empty without craft-fonts.
pub fn japanese_fonts() -> impl Iterator<Item = &'static CraftFont> {
    CRAFT_FONTS.iter().filter(|f| f.scripts.contains(&"Jpan"))
}

/// The TrueType or OpenType font inside a PresentationML embedded-font part
/// (`application/x-fontdata`).
///
/// The part is the font itself, or an Embedded OpenType wrapper around it (the `0x504C` magic
/// at byte 34, from the W3C Embedded OpenType submission). A MicroType Express subset is neither,
/// so this returns none; the original part stays in the file for the round trip.
pub fn embedded_sfnt(part: &[u8]) -> Option<&[u8]> {
    eot_payload(part).or_else(|| sfnt_or_collection(part).then_some(part))
}

fn sfnt_or_collection(b: &[u8]) -> bool {
    b.len() >= 12
        && (b.starts_with(&[0x00, 0x01, 0x00, 0x00])
            || b.starts_with(b"OTTO")
            || b.starts_with(b"true")
            || b.starts_with(b"typ1")
            || b.starts_with(b"ttcf"))
}

/// Font data at the end of an Embedded OpenType blob, when the header is one.
fn eot_payload(b: &[u8]) -> Option<&[u8]> {
    if b.len() < 82 || u16::from_le_bytes([b[34], b[35]]) != 0x504C {
        return None;
    }
    let version = u32::from_le_bytes(b.get(8..12)?.try_into().ok()?);
    if !matches!(version, 0x0001_0000 | 0x0002_0001 | 0x0002_0002) {
        return None;
    }
    let eot_size = u32::from_le_bytes(b.get(0..4)?.try_into().ok()?) as usize;
    let font_size = u32::from_le_bytes(b.get(4..8)?.try_into().ok()?) as usize;
    if font_size < 12 || eot_size < font_size.saturating_add(82) || eot_size > b.len() {
        return None;
    }
    let font = b.get(eot_size - font_size..eot_size)?;
    sfnt_or_collection(font).then_some(font)
}

/// Japanese faces in document-fallback order: Mincho (serif) families first, matching the
/// serif default text font, then the others; Regular before other styles.
pub fn japanese_document_fonts() -> Vec<&'static CraftFont> {
    let mut v: Vec<_> = japanese_fonts().collect();
    v.sort_by_key(|f| (!f.family.contains("Mincho"), f.style != "Regular"));
    v
}

Empty when neither exists.\npub fn craft_fonts() -> &'static [CraftFont] {\n    if !EMBEDDED_FONTS.is_empty() {\n        return EMBEDDED_FONTS;\n    }\n    #[cfg(target_arch = \"wasm32\")]\n    {\n        EMBEDDED_FONTS\n    }\n    #[cfg(not(target_arch = \"wasm32\"))]\n    {\n        static INSTALLED: std::sync::OnceLock<Vec<CraftFont>> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();\n        INSTALLED.get_or_init(|| {\n            let dir = std::env::var_os(\"MALUOS_FONTS_DIR\").map_or_else(|| std::path::PathBuf::from(INSTALLED_FONTS_DIR), std::path::PathBuf::from);\n            match installed_fonts(&dir) {\n                Ok(v) if v.is_empty() => {\n                    log::info!(\"no font catalogue in {} and none embedded: system fonts only\", dir.display());\n                    v\n                }\n                Ok(v) => {\n                    log::info!(\"{} faces from {}\", v.len(), dir.display());\n                    v\n                }\n                Err(e) => {\n                    log::warn!(\"font catalogue in {} not loaded: {e}\", dir.display());\n                    Vec::new()\n                }\n            }\n        })\n    }\n}\n\n/// Read an installed catalogue: `manifest.txt` in `dir` with one `family | style | file |\n/// scripts` row per face (`#` comments; `file` relative to `dir`, `scripts` comma-separated\n/// ISO 15924), in order. No directory or manifest is an empty catalogue; a malformed row or an\n/// unreadable file is an error. The data stays for the process (leaked, as embedded bytes would).\n#[cfg(not(target_arch = \"wasm32\"))]\npub fn installed_fonts(dir: &std::path::Path) -> Result<Vec<CraftFont>, String> {\n    let manifest = dir.join(\"manifest.txt\");\n    let text = match std::fs::read_to_string(&manifest) {\n        Ok(t) => t,\n        Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => return Ok(Vec::new()),\n        Err(e) => return Err(format!(\"{}: {e}\", manifest.display())),\n    };\n    let leak = |s: &str| -> &'static str { Box::leak(s.to_owned().into_boxed_str()) };\n    let mut v = Vec::new();\n    for line in text.lines().map(str::trim).filter(|l| !l.is_empty() && !l.starts_with('#')) {\n        let f: Vec<&str> = line.split('|').map(str::trim).collect();\n        let [family, style, file, scripts] = f.as_slice() else {\n            return Err(format!(\"{}: malformed row: {line}\", manifest.display()));\n        };\n        if file.starts_with('/') || file.split('/').any(|part| part == \"..\") {\n            return Err(format!(\"{}: file outside the catalogue: {file}\", manifest.display()));\n        }\n        let path = dir.join(file);\n        let bytes = std::fs::read(&path).map_err(|e| format!(\"{}: {e}\", path.display()))?;\n        let scripts: Vec<&'static str> = scripts.split(',').map(str::trim).filter(|s| !s.is_empty()).map(leak).collect();\n        v.push(CraftFont {\n            family: leak(family),\n            style: leak(style),\n            scripts: Box::leak(scripts.into_boxed_slice()),\n            bytes: Box::leak(bytes.into_boxed_slice()),\n        });\n    }\n    Ok(v)\n}\n\n/// The craft-fonts faces for Japanese (`\"Jpan\"`), in manifest order. Empty without craft-fonts.\npub fn japanese_fonts() -> impl Iterator<Item = &'static CraftFont> {\n    craft_fonts().iter().filter(|f| f.scripts.contains(&\"Jpan\"))\n}\n'''\nassert s.count(a)==1\ns=s.replace(a,b)\ns=s.replace(\"/// A font from the optional craft-fonts build input (https://github.com/storytold/craft-fonts;\\n/// empty unless built with `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR`, see `build.rs`).\",\n            \"/// A font from the craft-fonts catalogue (https://github.com/storytold/craft-fonts): embedded\\n/// with `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR` (see `build.rs`) or read from the installed package ([`craft_fonts`]).\")\nopen(p,'w').write(s); print('lib.rs ok')\nEOF\ngrep -rn 'CRAFT_FONTS\\b' crates apps --include=*.rs | grep -v 'CRAFT_FONTS_' | head",

/// Glyph id of the first of `chars` the face has (0 = .notdef).
pub fn first_glyph(face: &FontFace, chars: &[char]) -> u32 {
    chars.iter().map(|c| face.glyph_for(*c)).find(|g| *g != 0).unwrap_or(0)
}

==== release.yml
# MaluOS Slides release: the Linux .deb and tarball, attached to the GitHub release of the tag.
# The MaluOS archive takes the .deb from here (plan step 2.6). Linux only (plan D1).
name: Release

on:
  push:
    tags: ["v*"]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: "Version override for a test run, e.g. 0.10.0-rc.1 (empty: Cargo.toml)"
        type: string
        default: ""

permissions:
  contents: write

concurrency:
  group: release-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  NFPM_VERSION: 2.48.0

jobs:
  linux:
    # Built on the oldest supported Ubuntu so the binaries run on newer glibc (MaluOS is 26.04).
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 90
    env:
      CRAFT_FONTS_DIR: ${{ github.workspace }}/craft-fonts
      CRAFT_FONTS_REQUIRED: "1"
      MALUOS_SLIDES_VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
      CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          repository: storytold/craft-fonts
          ref: aced4137c022f1f587624d48e81ec77e1914a9cc
          path: craft-fonts
      - name: Linux build dependencies and packaging tools
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
            libasound2-dev libxkbcommon-dev libwayland-dev libx11-dev libxrandr-dev libxi-dev \
            libgl1-mesa-dev pkg-config cmake desktop-file-utils appstream
          curl -fsSL -o nfpm.tar.gz "https://github.com/goreleaser/nfpm/releases/download/v${NFPM_VERSION}/nfpm_${NFPM_VERSION}_Linux_x86_64.tar.gz"
          curl -fsSL -o checksums.txt "https://github.com/goreleaser/nfpm/releases/download/v${NFPM_VERSION}/checksums.txt"
          grep " nfpm_${NFPM_VERSION}_Linux_x86_64.tar.gz$" checksums.txt | sed 's| .*| nfpm.tar.gz|' | sha256sum -c -
          sudo tar -xzf nfpm.tar.gz -C /usr/local/bin nfpm
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
      - name: Build and package
        run: packaging/linux/package.sh --formats "deb tar"
      - name: Checksums
        run: cd dist/release && sha256sum * > SHA256SUMS.txt && cat SHA256SUMS.txt
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: maluos-slides-linux-x86_64
          path: dist/release/*
      - name: GitHub release
        if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
        uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v2
        with:
          files: dist/release/*
          generate_release_notes: true

## 🤖 Claude

Steps 2.6 and 2.8 are landed and pushed in both repositories. Step 2.7, the boot test, is running in the MaluOS CI now and I'll report its result when it finishes.

**Step 2.8, fonts decision (commit `aec215df` here, `aabae37` in maludb/maluos).** The measurement from 2.6 settled it: each Slides binary embedded 80 MB of fonts, and Malu123 ships none at all. The fonts now ship once as a shared package.

- A new script in `packaging/linux/fonts-package.sh` builds `maluos-fonts` from the craft-fonts checkout. It applies the same family exclusions as the build script, writes a catalogue file in fallback order, and carries the 26 licence files and a copyright file listing all 56 faces. The deb is 28 MB.
- The fonts crate now reads that catalogue at start when built with `CRAFT_FONTS_EMBED=0`. Every place that used the embedded table, including the fallback order and the interface fonts, goes through one accessor, so nothing changes behaviourally. Builds outside MaluOS and the web build keep embedding.
- Proof: the sample deck and a test deck with Japanese, Chinese, Korean, Arabic, Hebrew, Devanagari, Georgian and symbols render byte-identical with fonts embedded and with the no-embed build reading the package. All 18 images matched. Two of them are in the status file as screenshots.
- The Slides deb dropped from 88 MB to 31 MB. The gate passed with all 8 steps green, including a new unit test for the catalogue reader.
- In the MaluOS repo: the fonts deb is vendored with its refresh script, the desktop seed depends on it, the metapackage is at 0.2.16, and the Slides deb is re-vendored without fonts. The desktop boot test now checks that Malu123, Slides and the fonts are installed, that the Slides entry is in the Office category, that `.pptx` opens with it, and that fontconfig sees the fonts.

The decision is recorded as D5 revised in the plan and as design-record row H36 for Malu123 and MaluDocs.

**Step 2.7, boot test.** The MaluOS images workflow with the desktop input builds the desktop image and boots it under KVM with the new checks. I dispatched it on the new commit and am waiting for it. An earlier dispatch on the previous commit is also still running. Note that the Slides CI on GitHub stays red until the workflow pin lands, see below.

**Still yours.** Two uncommitted workflow files in this repo wait for a token with the `workflow` scope: the craft-fonts pin in both workflows, and in the release workflow the no-embed switch plus the fonts package step. Run once, then commit and push them:

```
gh auth refresh -h github.com -s workflow
```

Installing on this desk needs sudo, both packages together:

```
sudo apt install ./dist/release/maluos-fonts_2026.10.25-1_all.deb ./dist/release/maluos-slides-0.15.0-linux-x86_64.deb
```

==== gaps windows/mac sections
### Startup crashes on some Windows GPUs (#40, #59)
- **Evidence:** #59 (Intel UHD, access violation in `igvk64.dll` during Vulkan enumeration), #40
  (WordCraft, GridCraft and MaluOS Slides all fail on one Windows 11 PC). The DX12 default (#16) fixed
  AMD's `atio6axx.dll` crash only.
- **Impact:** the app never opens for those users.
- **Estimate:** 4–8 h (backend probing outside the process or a safe-mode fallback, a software
  renderer path). Needs a tester with the hardware. **Beta blocker.**

- **Impact:** copy-paste of screenshots is a core workflow.
- **Estimate:** 2–4 h. **Beta blocker.**

Every known shortfall, one entry each, ranked by how much it stops someone who presents with
PowerPoint from switching. This is the work list: pick from the top. Numbers are summarized in
[target-app-parity.md](target-app-parity.md); the feature-by-feature scores are in
[parity-checklist.md](parity-checklist.md). Hours are Opus 5.5 agent wall-clock hours including
tests (calibration in [target-app-parity.md](target-app-parity.md#calibration-how-the-hours-were-derived)).

[alpha gate](roadmap.md#alpha-gate-powerpoints-core-workflows).

MaluOS Slides aims at full PowerPoint parity, and to be better: faster, open (a documented zip+JSON
format plus PPTX), scriptable by agents (CLI, JSON control channel, MCP), and available everywhere
(macOS, Windows, Linux, BSD and the web). This page is the summary; the detail is in
[docs/target-app-parity.md](docs/target-app-parity.md) and the work list in
[docs/gaps.md](docs/gaps.md).

use super::{Color32, CornerRadius, Rect, Sense, SlideApp, Stroke, Tokens, Ui, pos2, theme, vec2};

/// Room the About credits need for their table; the About tab keeps its compact size.
pub(super) const CREDITS_SIZE: egui::Vec2 = vec2(640.0, 380.0);

/// The Contributors / Models body in a block of its own fixed size, below the tab row. Sizing the
/// dialog's `ui` instead (`set_min_size` / `set_max_height`) squeezed the tab row and the first
/// credits row together, so the text was garbled and the tabs stopped answering (#843).
pub(super) fn credits_block(ui: &mut Ui, models: bool) -> Rect {
    ui.allocate_ui(CREDITS_SIZE, |ui| {
        ui.set_min_size(CREDITS_SIZE);
        if models { crate::credits::models_ui(ui) } else { crate::credits::contributors_ui(ui) }
    })
    .response
    .rect
}

pub fn about(_app: &mut SlideApp, ui: &mut Ui) {
    let t = Tokens::get(ui.ctx());
    ui.vertical_centered(|ui| {
        let (r, _) = ui.allocate_exact_size(vec2(64.0, 64.0), Sense::hover());
        paint_logo(ui.painter(), r);
        ui.label(egui::RichText::new("MaluOS Slides").font(theme::bold(22.0)));
        ui.label(egui::RichText::new(version_line()).color(t.text_dim));
        ui.add_space(6.0);
        ui.label("The MaluOS presentation app, a fork of DeckCraft by the ArtCraft team.");
        ui.label("An open-source, clean-room project. Not affiliated with Microsoft.");
        ui.add_space(6.0);
        ui.hyperlink_to("Discussions on GitHub", maluos_slides_engine::links::DISCORD);
        ui.hyperlink_to("github.com/maludb/maluos-slides", maluos_slides_engine::links::APP_PAGE);
}

/// MaluOS Slides' mark, drawn in code: a slide card with a play triangle in our orange.
pub fn paint_logo(p: &egui::Painter, r: Rect) {
    let orange = Color32::from_rgb(0xF2, 0x6B, 0x1D);
    let deep = Color32::from_rgb(0xC2, 0x4E, 0x14);
    let card = r.shrink(r.width() * 0.08);
    p.rect_filled(card.translate(vec2(r.width() * 0.04, r.width() * 0.05)), CornerRadius::same((r.width() * 0.14) as u8), deep);
    p.rect_filled(card, CornerRadius::same((r.width() * 0.14) as u8), orange);
    let c = card.center();
    let s = card.width() * 0.22;
    p.add(egui::Shape::convex_polygon(
        vec![pos2(c.x - s * 0.7, c.y - s), pos2(c.x + s, c.y), pos2(c.x - s * 0.7, c.y + s)],
        Color32::WHITE,
        Stroke::NONE,
    ));
}

## 🤖 Claude

Here is where things stand while that run goes.

**Done this turn and pushed.**

- **Icon and logo** (commit `0b689e6e`). Your MaluSlidesIcon image is now the app icon in every size, the scalable entry, the Windows and web `.ico`, and the About box and Backstage logo. The original is kept in the repo as the source, and a new command, `cargo xtask icons`, derives everything from it, so the next swap is one command. It is attributed as a MaluOS brand asset and recorded as decision D13 and design-record row H37. The 2.5 screenshot shows the About box with the new mark. The Slides deb in the MaluOS repo was rebuilt and re-vendored with the new icon.
- **Phase 6 planned** (commit `aa69e48c`). The inherited work list and roadmap are pruned to Linux and MaluOS. Eight steps are picked in order: no data loss, SVG pictures, printing, presenter view on the second display, vector PDF, media options, font faces, a real-deck corpus.
- Every gate run was green.

**Step 2.7, the boot test.** The first full run passed every Slides check: both apps and the fonts installed, Office category, `.pptx` association, the CLI answers. The one failure of mine was a wrong face count, fixed. Three other failures were the platform's own idle-mark timing checks, which have nothing to do with Slides and passed on the last successful desktop run on 2026-10-23. Two reruns were then cancelled by the workflow's own rule, which cancels an in-progress image run whenever a new push lands. A final run on the finished tree is in flight now, and I'll record 2.7 when it reports.

**Still yours.**

- The two workflow files with the craft-fonts pin and the no-embed release step stay uncommitted until you run `gh auth refresh -h github.com -s workflow`, then commit and push them. The Slides CI on GitHub stays red until then.
